head: e0a9ce03c8c1cc839eaf409e2677b9abf2017b1f
title: Implement Global Date Notes
body:
This PR implements the global date note feature, allowing users to attach descriptive notes to specific dates in their travel itinerary. These notes are displayed in the Planner view alongside scheduled locations.

closes #151 

---

## Description

This PR fully develops the `note` command and integrates it with the UI and storage layers. Unlike locations, notes are global to the date and provide a general description or reminder for that day's plan.

**Key Changes:**
- **Global Storage:** Notes are now stored in a centralized `Map<VisitDate, NoteContent>` within the `AddressBook`, making them independent of individual location records.
- **Reactive UI:** The `PlannerListPanel` now dynamically observes a `plannerNote` property in the `Model`. When a user runs the `plan` command, the UI automatically updates to show the relevant note.
- **Smart Note Merging:** If multiple notes apply to the same date (e.g., a specific date note and a recurring "Every Friday" note), they are intelligently merged and displayed together.
- **Persistence:** Global notes are serialized into `addressbook.json` and persist across application restarts.
- **Undo/Redo Support:** The `note` command is now fully undoable, integrated into the application's state-snapshot mechanism.

---

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] Backend implementation (fulfilling deferred functionality)
- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Documentation update (Implementation details in Developer Guide)

---

## Test Coverage
- ✅ **Unit Tests:** Updated `NoteCommandTest` to verify backend execution and `AddressBookTest` for map serialization.
- ✅ **Mocking:** Updated `ModelStub` in `AddCommandTest` to support new interface methods.
- ✅ **Integration Tests:** Verified that `NoteCommand` correctly modifies the model and triggers UI-bound properties.

### Manual Testing Verification
- `note n/buy souvenir d/2026-03-24` → Success message shown.
- `plan 2026-03-24` → Planner sidebar displays "buy souvenir".
- `undo` → Note disappears from the active planner view.
- Restart App → `plan 2026-03-24` still shows the saved note.
- `note n/Weekly check d/every Tuesday` → Note displays every Tuesday in the planner.


---

## Checklist for Reviewers

- [x] Code follows the project's coding style (Checkstyle passed)
- [x] Comments and documentation are clear and accurate
- [x] All tests pass locally
- [x] New feature is fully integrated with Undo/Redo
- [x] Storage uses `toDataString()` to ensure robust cross-session loading
- [x] UI placeholder "TEST" removed and replaced with live data bindings
- [x] Multiple notes for the same `LocalDate` handle string joining correctly

---

## Future Enhancements

Possible improvements for future iterations:
- Implementation of `DeleteNoteCommand` (currently deferred)
- Support for rich text or bullet points in notes
- Adding an "Edit Note" button directly in the Planner UI
- Visual indicators/icons in the list view for dates that have notes attached

head: fbdecd6bd0b3148b84d91b6c4eff3c6d7ce54198
title: feat: EXP-V1-0004 documentation and context engineering standard
body:
## Summary

- **EXP-V1-0004 (parent)**: Configurable context engineering for a project's technical documentation directory. Enforces structured docs with frontmatter-driven indexing — every `.md` file has YAML front matter, every directory has a `README.md` with auto-generated `## Index` tables. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md context files per directory for AI agents. Root-level context files referencing documentation location. All configurable via `.apss/config.toml` with zero-config defaults.
- **EXP-V1-0004.ADR01 (substandard)**: Enforces Architecture Decision Records — `ADR-XXX-<name>.md` naming (3-5 digit numbers), required front matter (`name`, `description`, `status`), Fowler lifecycle (`proposed`/`accepted`/`deprecated`/`superseded`), keyword-based required ADRs, required `## Context/Decision/Consequences` headers, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md with backlinking guidance, dead ADR reference detection, and superseded/deprecated reference warnings.
- **CLI integration**: `aps run docs validate` and `aps run docs index` commands that run both parent and substandard, merging diagnostics. Central standard registry eliminates magic strings.

### Error codes

| Parent (DOC) | Substandard (ADR01) |
|---|---|
| MISSING_README | ADR01-001 Missing ADR directory |
| MISSING_CLAUDE_MD | ADR01-002 Invalid naming |
| MISSING_AGENTS_MD | ADR01-003 Missing front matter |
| MISSING_INDEX | ADR01-004 Required keyword not satisfied |
| STALE_INDEX | ADR01-005 Reserved |
| MISSING_ROOT_CLAUDE_MD | ADR01-006 Invalid naming regex |
| MISSING_ROOT_AGENTS_MD | ADR01-007 Missing context file |
| MISSING_DOCS_REFERENCE | ADR01-008 Context file lacks guidance |
| | ADR01-009 Dead ADR reference |
| | ADR01-010 Missing required header |
| | ADR01-011 Missing/invalid status |
| | ADR01-012 Superseded/deprecated reference |

### Key design decisions

- **ADR_STEM_PATTERN** as single source of truth for all ADR regex patterns (`ADR-\d{3,5}-[a-zA-Z0-9-]+`)
- ADR status follows Fowler lifecycle — ADRs are never revised, only superseded
- Parent spec focuses on general docs structure; ADR details live in substandard

### Test coverage

- 5 config unit tests (stem pattern, filename pattern, keyword pattern, metacharacter escaping)
- 12 parent integration tests (config, frontmatter, index, readme)
- 14 ADR unit tests (error codes, reference extraction, header matching, status validation, digit range)
- 28 ADR integration tests across 7 fixture scenarios

- [x] `cargo test -p documentation-adr` — all pass (14 unit + 28 integration)

head: c58a06a5a4eb45ccfffb8c0ba75306d559482b39
title: fix: six firmware bugs found in line-by-line audit
body:
## Summary

Fixes 6 bugs found during a comprehensive line-by-line audit of both the sonde-node and sonde-modem firmware.

---

### Bug 1: Factory reset doesn't clear stored WiFi channel
**File:** `key_store.rs`

After factory reset + re-pairing with a different gateway on a different channel, the node used the **stale channel** from the previous pairing and couldn't communicate. Now clears channel to default (channel 1) on factory reset.

### Bug 2: Modem bridge doesn't reset frame decoder on USB reconnect
**File:** `bridge.rs`

When USB reconnects, `MODEM_READY` was sent but the `FrameDecoder` was **not** reset. Stale partial frame bytes from before the disconnect corrupted the first frames from the gateway. Now calls `decoder.reset()` on reconnect, matching the existing `handle_reset()` behavior.

### Bug 3: Zero sleep interval causes tight wake-sleep loop
**File:** `sleep.rs`, `wake_cycle.rs`

`UpdateSchedule { interval_s: 0 }` from the gateway or `set_next_wake(0)` from BPF caused `enter_deep_sleep(0)` ΓåÆ immediate wake ΓåÆ infinite loop that drains the battery in hours. Now clamps `effective_sleep_s()` to a minimum of 1 second.

### Bug 4: Dead `resolve_map_references` code
**File:** `program_store.rs`

The function and 3 tests were left over from the rbpf era. LDDW `src=1` map reference relocation is now handled by the `sonde_bpf` interpreter at runtime. Removed ~70 lines of dead code and 3 dead tests.

### Bug 5: Zero-size maps cause HashMap key collision in BPF dispatch
**File:** `map_storage.rs`

Two maps with `max_entries=0` produce identical `data_ptr()` values (Rust's dangling pointer for empty `Vec`). This caused the dispatch context's `map_ptr_index` HashMap to silently overwrite one entry, making `map_lookup_elem`/`map_update_elem` access the wrong map. Now rejects `max_entries == 0` and `value_size == 0` in `validate_map_defs()`.

### Bug 6: Inconsistent zero-length check in I2C write-read helper
**File:** `bpf_dispatch.rs`

`helper_i2c_read` and `helper_i2c_write` reject `len == 0`, but `helper_i2c_write_read` allowed zero-length for both `write_len` and `read_len`. A BPF program could bypass the zero-length check by using the combined helper. Now consistently rejects zero-length transfers.

---

## Testing

- 144 tests pass across sonde-node and sonde-modem (0 failures)
- 4 new tests added (2 for min-sleep clamp, 2 for zero-size map rejection)
- 3 dead tests removed (for the deleted `resolve_map_references`)
- Clippy clean with `-D warnings`

Fixes #127

head: 78f6157eaec39a413d216616a44734ac53df3d6e
title: Fix incomplete CRUD, stale form state, and missing delete-activity test from PR #8
body:
PR #8 implemented `useInventory` with full CRUD including `updateItem`, but the hook's Update path was never wired to the UI, the Add modal leaked form state across open/close cycles, and the delete activity side-effect had no test coverage.

## Changes

- **Complete the Update path (`updateItem`)**
  - `AddItemModal` gains optional `editItem` / `onUpdate` props; toggles title and submit label between *Add New Item* / *Edit Item* modes
  - `InventoryTable` adds a per-row **Edit** button (cyan, beside Delete)
  - `InventoryPage` manages `editingItem` state and a unified `openModal(item?)` helper
  - `App.tsx` now destructures and passes `updateItem` down to `InventoryPage`

- **Form reset on modal close**  
  A `modalKey` counter in `InventoryPage` increments on every `openModal()` call, forcing React to remount `AddItemModal` fresh — no residual state from a cancelled session. Edit mode pre-fills via a `useState` function initializer.

  ```tsx
  // InventoryPage.tsx
  const openModal = (item?: InventoryItem) => {
    setEditingItem(item)
    setModalKey(prev => prev + 1)   // force remount → clean form
    setIsModalOpen(true)
  }

  <AddItemModal key={modalKey} editItem={editingItem} onUpdate={onUpdate} ... />
  ```

- **Missing test: delete creates activity**  
  Added `'adds activity when deleting an item'` to `useInventory.test.ts`; asserts `activities` grows by 1 with `action: 'removed'` and the correct `itemName`.

head: 1e8d2e2f880cfe1d9bcbdfbc6078cb6b72fd35ce
title: Add stream media source
body:
<!--
 Hello, and thank you for your interest in contributing to the .NET MAUI Toolkit! 

 Before you submit please check that this work relates to one of the following:
 - Bug fix
    If you haven't yet opened an Issue that reports the bug in detail, provides a reproduction sample, and has been verified + reproduced by a member of the .NET MAUI Toolkit core team, please do that before submitting a Pull Request.
 - Feature/Proposal
    If you haven't yet submitted a Proposal that has been Championed by a .NET MAUI core team member, please instead open a Discussion at https://github.com/communitytoolkit/maui/discussions/new where we can discuss the pros/cons of the feature and its implementation. 
 Any PR submitted that does not fit with the above options will be closed.
 -->

 ### Description of Change ###

Adds StreamMediaSource support to MediaElement so media can be played directly from a .NET Stream.

This is intended for scenarios where media should remain in memory or within the app sandbox, rather than being written out to a file or fetched from an external URL. It enables workflows such as capturing or generating media in-memory and previewing it before persisting it.

The change adds a new MediaSource subtype and wires it through the existing MediaElement pipeline on supported platforms:
- Windows: uses WinMediaSource.CreateFromStream with IRandomAccessStream conversion
- Android: uses a custom ExoPlayer IDataSource implementation backed by Stream
- iOS/macOS: uses AVAssetResourceLoader to serve stream data to AVPlayer
- Tizen: explicitly reports stream playback as unsupported

The API follows the existing MediaSource patterns, including a MediaSource.FromStream(Stream) factory method and direct use of StreamMediaSource.

 <!-- Describe your changes here. This only needs to be brief as the linked issues below will already cover the detailed changes. -->

 ### Linked Issues ###
 <!-- Provide links to issues here (#35 will link to issue number 35). Ensure that a GitHub issue was created for your bug/proposal and it has been approved/Championed. -->

- Related discussion: https://github.com/CommunityToolkit/Maui/discussions/2968

 ### PR Checklist ###
 <!--
 Please check all the things you did here and double-check that you got it all, or state why you didn't do something.

 If anything is unclear please do ask :)
 -->
 - [x] Has a linked Issue, and the Issue has been `approved`(bug) or `Championed` (feature/proposal)
         **Note:** Has a linked discussion, not issue, however was discussed and approved by @TheCodeTraveler, @ne0rrmatrix and @VladislavAntonyuk  on the standup today (see: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gF1YSJyxAB8)
 - [x] Has tests (if omitted, state reason in description)
 - [x] Has samples (if omitted, state reason in description)
 - [x] Rebased on top of `main` at time of PR
 - [x] Changes adhere to [coding standard](https://github.com/CommunityToolkit/Maui/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code---best-practices)
 - [x] Documentation created or updated: https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/CommunityToolkit/pull/642


 ### Additional information ###

 <!-- 
 Please use this to aid the reviewer, this could include stating which platform(s) have been tested
 -->
 

- This work is currently linked to discussion 2968 rather than a formal issue.
- The feature proposal originated from secure-app scenarios where media must remain in-memory and within the app sandbox.
- Sample app updates are included to demonstrate stream-backed playback.
- Tizen is not supported at this stage and reports that limitation explicitly.
- Tested platforms: Windows, Android, iOS/macOS as applicable to the implementation.


## What Was Added

### Core Class
- **`StreamMediaSource.shared.cs`**: New `MediaSource` subclass that wraps a .NET `Stream`
  - Includes `Stream` bindable property
  - Implicit operators for convenient Stream conversion
  - Factory method `MediaSource.FromStream(Stream)`
  - Follows the same pattern as `FileMediaSource`, `UriMediaSource`, and `ResourceMediaSource`

### Platform-Specific Implementations

#### Windows (`MediaManager.windows.cs`)
- **Implementation**: Uses `WinMediaSource.CreateFromStream()` with `IRandomAccessStream`
- **Status**: ✅ Fully Supported
- **Method**: Leverages `WindowsRuntimeStreamExtensions.AsRandomAccessStream()` to convert .NET streams to Windows Runtime streams
- **Helper**: `StreamExtensions.windows.cs` - Provides `GetMimeType()` extension method

#### Android (`MediaManager.android.cs`)
- **Implementation**: Custom `StreamDataSource` implementing ExoPlayer's `IDataSource` interface
- **Status**: ✅ Fully Supported
- **Method**: Created custom data source that reads from .NET Stream and integrates with ExoPlayer's `ProgressiveMediaSource`
- **Helper**: `StreamDataSource.android.cs` - Contains `StreamDataSource` and `StreamDataSourceFactory` classes
- **Features**:
  - Supports seeking if stream is seekable
  - Handles range requests
  - Proper resource cleanup and disposal

#### iOS/macOS (`MediaManager.macios.cs`)
- **Implementation**: Uses `AVAssetResourceLoaderDelegate` to provide custom data source
- **Status**: ✅ Fully Supported
- **Method**: Creates custom URL scheme (`stream://media`) and uses `AVAssetResourceLoader` to intercept loading requests
- **Helper**: `StreamAssetResourceLoader.macios.cs` - Custom delegate that feeds stream data to `AVPlayer`
- **Features**:
  - Works with both audio and video
  - Supports seeking if stream is seekable
  - Integrates seamlessly with existing `AVPlayer` architecture

#### Tizen (`MediaManager.tizen.cs`)
- **Status**: ❌ Not Supported
- **Reason**: Platform limitation - throws `NotSupportedException` with helpful message

## Usage Examples

```csharp
// Using factory method
MediaSource source = MediaSource.FromStream(myStream);

// Using implicit conversion
MediaSource source = myStream;

// Direct instantiation
var streamSource = new StreamMediaSource { Stream = myStream };

// Assigning to MediaElement
mediaElement.Source = MediaSource.FromStream(myStream);
```

## Files Modified

### New Files
1. `MediaSource/StreamMediaSource.shared.cs` - Core class
2. `Platforms/Android/StreamDataSource.android.cs` - Android implementation
3. `Views/StreamAssetResourceLoader.macios.cs` - iOS/macOS implementation
4. `Views/StreamExtensions.windows.cs` - Windows helper extensions

### Modified Files
1. `MediaSource/MediaSource.shared.cs` - Added `FromStream()` factory method
2. `Views/MediaManager.android.cs` - Added stream support via custom DataSource
3. `Views/MediaManager.windows.cs` - Added stream support via `CreateFromStream()`
4. `Views/MediaManager.macios.cs` - Added stream support via `AVAssetResourceLoader`
5. `Views/MediaManager.tizen.cs` - Added NotSupportedException for streams
6. `Converters/MediaSourceConverter.shared.cs` - Added `StreamMediaSource` case

## Technical Details

### Android Implementation
The Android implementation uses ExoPlayer's extensibility model:
- `StreamDataSource` implements `IDataSource` interface
- Reads data from .NET Stream on demand
- `StreamDataSourceFactory` creates instances for ExoPlayer
- Integrates with `ProgressiveMediaSource.Factory`

### iOS/macOS Implementation
The iOS/macOS implementation uses Apple's official extension mechanism:
- Creates `AVUrlAsset` with custom URL scheme
- `AVAssetResourceLoaderDelegate` intercepts resource loading requests
- Provides stream data through `AVAssetResourceLoadingDataRequest`
- Supports both content information and data requests

### Windows Implementation
The Windows implementation uses built-in .NET stream conversion:
- Converts .NET Stream to `IRandomAccessStream` using `AsRandomAccessStream()`
- Uses `WinMediaSource.CreateFromStream()` API
- Provides default MIME type (can be enhanced for better type detection)

## Considerations

### Stream Lifecycle
- Streams are **not** automatically disposed by the MediaElement
- Callers are responsible for managing stream lifetime
- Consider keeping streams open for the duration of playback
- Seeking requires seekable streams

### MIME Type Detection
- Windows: Returns generic `"application/octet-stream"` by default
- iOS/macOS: Defaults to `"video/mp4"` assumption
- Future enhancement: Could detect MIME type from stream content (magic bytes)

### Performance
- Streams should support efficient random access for best performance
- Non-seekable streams may have limited functionality
- Consider buffering strategies for network streams

## Future Enhancements

1. **MIME Type Detection**: Implement magic byte detection to automatically determine content type
2. **Tizen Support**: Investigate if Tizen platform can support stream-based playback
3. **Stream Properties**: Add optional properties to `StreamMediaSource` for MIME type hint
4. **Buffering Options**: Add configurable buffering strategies for different stream types
5. **Progress Reporting**: Add stream read progress callbacks for monitoring

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> I want to convert Fortran codebases to Rust using an automated conversion pipeline that leverages LLM. The pipeline has to ensure numerical accuracy between the Fortran and Rust code and achieve comparable or better performance. The first codebase is BLAS, where the first milestone is full or near-full automation of the dgemm function. The second is to go to 10 functions, and the last one is the full library.
> 
> This repository should allow someone to clone it, run a Rust conversion of the specified Fortran database code, and, optionally, for the specified subset only, receive a post-conversion report on accuracy and performance, along with the converted code.
> 
> I want to explore 3 ideas.
> 1. An LLM-first, rule-fallback.
> The core idea is to let an LLM do the heavy lifting; invoke a rule‑based transpiler only when the LLM fails to compile.
> The steps are:
>   a. Pre‑process – split Fortran into ≤ 200‑line functions, strip comments, build a call‑graph.
>   b. LLM translate – feed each function to LLM or another with a prompt that supplies external vars & intrinsics.
>   c. Compile & repair – run rustc; feed errors back to the LLM for up to 2 repair rounds.
>   d. Unit‑test round‑trip – auto‑generate Fortran‑style unit tests, run both versions, compare outputs.
>   e. Package – glue functions into a Cargo crate, run cargo test.
> Tools/Prompts:
>   - Tree‑sitter‑fortran or fparser for parsing
>   - LLM API (Start open‑source, but allow paid, like my GitHub Copilot)
>   - rustc/cargo
>   - Simple Python harness for test generation
> 
> 2. An Agentic multi‑turn dialogue.
> The core idea is to use a Questioner‑Solver agent pair (as in LLMigrate & Fortran2CPP) to catch semantic mistakes that pure one‑shot LLMs miss.
> The steps are:
>   a. Chunk & embed – same preprocessing as idea 1.
>   b. Solver – LLM proposes Rust translation.
>   c. Questioner – second LLM (or same model with a different prompt) asks clarifying questions about Fortran intrinsics, implicit typing, and module interfaces; the Solver revises.
>   d. Compile‑test loop – as in idea 1.
>   e. Idiomization pass – run a Rust‑clippy‑like script to replace unsafe blocks with safe idioms where possible.
>   f. Final audit – spot‑check < 15 % of lines.
> Tools/prompts:
>   - Two‑prompt LLM pipeline (can be done with a single model via role‑play)
>   - Same parsing & build tools as Plan 1
>   - Clippy / miri for safety checks
> 
> 3. Hybrid rule‑based + LLM polishing
> The core idea is to start with a deterministic Fortran‑to‑Rust transpiler (e.g., f2c‑style or a custom regex‑based tool) to get a compilable skeleton, then let an LLM refine idioms and ownership.
> The steps are:
>   a. Rule‑based skeleton – run a quick Fortran‑to‑C transpiler (e.g., f2c) followed by a C‑to‑Rust tool (c2rust) to produce unsafe Rust.
>   b. LLM polish – feed each unsafe function to an LLM with a prompt to replace raw pointers with Rust references, lifetimes, and proper error handling.
>   c. Compile & test – same as idea 1.
>   d. Benchmark sanity‑check – run a lightweight performance kernel (e.g., matrix‑multiply) to ensure no major regression.
>   e. Document – generate Rustdoc comments from original Fortran comments.
> Tools/prompts:
>   - f2c (or f2c‑like)
>   - c2rust (or a simple C→Rust regex mapper)
>   - LLM for polishing
>   - cargo bench/criterion for quick perf check
> 
> Since this is a demo, add a script or an executable that launches the entire process, including fetching the BLAS library and prompting the user to choose what to convert: a single function, a sample of functions, or the entire library, and which idea to use for the conversion. During the conversion, there should be processing feedback, and, depending on the idea used, questions, similar to how GitHub Copilot CLI tool works. 


</details>

title: feat(cli): persist workflowDir in config and enforce full path for push
body:
## Summary

Addresses a recurring path confusion issue where AI agents would create workflow files in the wrong directory or pass a bare filename to `n8nac push`.

### Changes

**`config-service.ts`**
- Add `workflowDir` to `ILocalConfig` — computed as `<syncFolder>/<instanceIdentifier>/<projectSlug>` and persisted to `n8nac-config.json` automatically on every `instance add` / `instance select` / `init`.
- Agents can now read this field directly instead of reconstructing the path from the three component fields manually.

**`sync-manager.ts` — `resolvePushTarget`**
- Remove the basename-only shortcut: a bare filename (no `/`) was previously silently prefixed with the sync scope dir. Now it is resolved from `cwd` like any other relative path, so passing just `my-workflow.workflow.ts` fails immediately.
- Improved error message when path is outside scope: shows the active scope directory, the expected corrected path, and the exact corrected `n8nac push` command to run. Includes a tip pointing to `workflowDir` in `n8nac-config.json`.

**`ai-context-generator.ts` — AGENTS.md**
- Push step now mandates the full relative path form (`workflowDir/<file>.workflow.ts`).
- Remove the contradictory _"do not pass a path"_ bullet.
- `workflowDir` from the active instance in `n8nac-config.json` is the single source of truth for where to create and push workflow files — stable across `instance select` calls and `--instance` overrides.

head: c926adcf6e0be826e3313fc503a92b53a78f8ef8
title: Fix SMP scheduler evicting task when preemption is disabled
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1376 — SMP scheduler evicting a task that has preemption disabled via `vTaskPreemptionDisable()`.

In the SMP time-slicing path of `xTaskIncrementTick()`, `xYieldPendings[xCoreID]` was set to `pdTRUE` unconditionally without checking `xPreemptionDisable`. The later yield-processing block correctly skipped acting on it for preemption-disabled cores, but the **stale flag remained**. When a subsequent ISR (e.g. `xTaskGenericNotifyFromISR()`) called `prvYieldForTask()` — which correctly did not yield — it then checked `xYieldPendings[portGET_CORE_ID()]` and found the stale `pdTRUE`, erroneously setting `*pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken = pdTRUE`. This triggered `portYIELD_FROM_ISR()` → `vTaskSwitchContext()` → `prvSelectHighestPriorityTask()`, which evicted the preemption-disabled task.

## Changes (three-layer fix)

- **Root cause** (`xTaskIncrementTick`): Guard the time-slicing `xYieldPendings[]` assignment with a `configUSE_TASK_PREEMPTION_DISABLE` check so the flag is never set for cores running preemption-disabled tasks.

- **Defense in depth** (4 functions): In `xTaskResumeFromISR`, `xTaskRemoveFromEventList`, `xTaskGenericNotifyFromISR`, and `vTaskGenericNotifyGiveFromISR` — save `xYieldPendings[portGET_CORE_ID()]` before calling `prvYieldForTask()` and only report a yield if the flag transitioned from `pdFALSE` to `pdTRUE`. This eliminates false positives from any stale flags.

- **Safety net** (`vTaskSwitchContext` SMP path): Add a `xPreemptionDisable` check analogous to the existing `uxSchedulerSuspended` check. If a context switch is somehow triggered for a core whose task has preemption disabled, the switch is deferred (`xYieldPendings = pdTRUE`) and will execute when `vTaskPreemptionEnable()` calls `prvYieldCore()`.

## Configuration

Only affects SMP builds with:
```
configNUMBER_OF_CORES > 1
configUSE_TASK_PREEMPTION_DISABLE == 1
configUSE_PREEMPTION == 1
configUSE_TIME_SLICING == 1
```

Single-core builds are completely unaffected (all changes are inside `#if ( configNUMBER_OF_CORES > 1 )` or equivalent guards).

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify existing FreeRTOS SMP unit tests pass
- [ ] Test on dual-core SMP hardware (e.g. ESP32-S3) with preemption-disabled task + concurrent ISR notifications + same-priority time-slicing tasks (the scenario from #1376)
- [ ] Verify that preemption re-enablement (`vTaskPreemptionEnable`) still triggers deferred yields correctly
- [ ] Verify single-core builds are unaffected

head: fdc4ff8d1579a24e830cd636317d62d959eb0d40
title: Add saga reminder recovery runtime and operator surfaces +semver: breaking
body:
## Business Value



Saga recovery now has an explicit contract and runtime surface instead of hidden conventions. The work on this branch makes replay intent visible in code, gives the runtime stable execution metadata, persists authoritative recovery checkpoints, enforces resource-level access on operator surfaces, and adds generated client manual-resume support so consumers do not need handwritten plumbing.



**Key benefits:**



1. Saga authors must declare forward recovery intent explicitly.

2. Compensatable steps now fail build-time validation when compensation recovery policy is omitted or contradictory.

3. Runtime orchestration receives execution-context metadata that later reminder/manual-resume work can build on safely.

4. Saga orchestration now emits explicit execution-start markers and correlates follow-on saga progress events with durable attempt metadata.

5. Saga-level recovery intent is now emitted into runtime DI, persisted on saga-start events, participates in workflow identity hashing, and seeds a framework-owned checkpoint sidecar that can be rebuilt deterministically from saga infrastructure events.

6. Runtime recovery code can now load the latest persisted checkpoint through a dedicated accessor instead of re-deriving snapshot-key details at every future reminder/resume call site.

7. Blocked reminder/manual resume attempts now have a first-class infrastructure event that rebuilds operator-visible blocked state directly into the checkpoint model.

8. Runtime recovery now has a pure planning seam that compares workflow hashes, interprets checkpoint cursors, and decides whether to execute a step, block, complete, compensate, or no-op before reminder plumbing lands.

9. Runtime recovery now has an async coordinator seam that loads saga state plus the authoritative checkpoint and delegates decision-making to the planner without pushing reminder logic into the generic aggregate grain.

10. Runtime recovery can now execute those actionable decisions through an explicit internal resume command path that reuses in-flight attempt identity, emits replay markers for reminder/manual resumes, and keeps initial orchestration behavior unchanged.

11. Saga reminder lifecycle is now reconciled against persisted recovery state on activation, after state transitions, and after handled reminder ticks, with runtime kill switches and bounded automatic-attempt ceilings.

12. Generated saga HTTP surfaces now expose a metadata-only runtime-status route plus a typed manual-resume route backed by a public recovery service contract, while existing raw-state reads stay available separately.

13. Reminder review hardening now avoids unnecessary reminder-registry access for inapplicable recovery shapes, converts workflow mismatches into durable blocked reminder outcomes instead of letting stale reminder ticks churn forever, and avoids double reminder reconciliation when a handled reminder tick already executed a command.

14. Generated MCP saga tooling now adds a metadata-only runtime-status tool plus a destructive manual-resume tool that both reuse the public recovery service seam and return typed JSON instead of prose-only operator responses.

15. Generated saga client features now support manual resume commands with typed `SagaResumeResponse` handling and generated reducer/effect registration so UI flows can trigger operator resumes without handwritten plumbing.

16. Saga runtime-status and manual-resume surfaces now fail closed using stored/current caller-context fingerprints, with a default resource-level authorizer and a typed `Unauthorized` manual-resume outcome.

17. Spring sample money-transfer status projections and operator UI now surface recovery metadata end to end, including blocked-state visibility and a typed manual Resume Transfer action.

18. Projection client and gateway generators now correctly emit nullable enum DTOs and mapper conversions so recovery metadata like pending direction and last resume source compile cleanly in generated projection surfaces.

19. Generated saga-status reducers now cover execution-started, blocked-resume, and compensation-progress recovery events so projection read models stay aligned with the framework recovery model.
20. Docusaurus saga and Spring sample docs now reflect the recovery-aware step contracts, runtime-status/manual-resume surfaces, and a public upgrade guide for pre-0.0.1 saga code.



## Common Use Cases



| Domain | Use Case | Example |

|--------|----------|---------|

| Payments | Mark non-idempotent steps as manual-only | A money-transfer debit step can block automatic replay until operators confirm recovery behavior. |

| Workflow orchestration | Carry execution metadata into step code | A step can inspect `SagaStepExecutionContext` for direction, source, and operation identity. |

| Tooling and CI | Fail fast on unsafe saga declarations | A compensatable step without `CompensationRecoveryPolicy` now produces a targeted generator error. |

| Client UX | Trigger operator-driven resume without handwritten HTTP wiring | Generated saga client features now dispatch typed manual-resume actions/effects and store the latest `SagaResumeResponse`. |

| Multi-tenant operations | Restrict status/resume to the current caller scope | Stored access fingerprints can deny raw-state reads, runtime-status reads, and manual resume when the caller fingerprint does not match. |

| Sample operations | Show blocked/manual resume end to end | Spring money-transfer operations now display recovery mode, pending step, blocked reason, last resume metadata, and a Resume Transfer action when manual intervention is required. |

| Projection generation | Preserve nullable recovery enums in generated DTOs | Projection generators now emit DTO enums and mapper casts for nullable fields such as `PendingDirection` and `LastResumeSource`. |
| Documentation and migrations | Explain the new contracts with before/after guidance | The docs set now includes a public upgrade guide plus updated Spring tutorials for recovery-aware saga code. |



## How It Works



### Overview



This branch lays the contract, planner, runtime, and generated-surface foundation for saga recovery:



```text

Saga step attribute -> generator validation -> SagaStepInfo metadata -> runtime execution context

                                    -> recovery checkpoint + planner/coordinator

                                    -> HTTP / MCP / client manual-resume surfaces

```



### Key Design Decisions



- **Runtime-owned recovery contracts**: recovery enums/attributes/context live in `DomainModeling.Abstractions`, not generator-only packages.

- **Compiler/analyzer-first enforcement**: forward policy is a required `SagaStepAttribute<TSaga>` constructor argument, and compensation rules are validated during saga registration generation.

- **Metadata-first runtime plumbing**: `SagaStepInfo` and step hashing now carry recovery policy data, and `SagaOrchestrationEffect` passes `SagaStepExecutionContext` into step execution.

- **Checkpoint access seam**: the runtime now has a focused `SagaRecoveryCheckpointAccessor<TSaga>` that uses the saga brook cursor plus the checkpoint reducer hash to load the latest checkpoint snapshot deterministically.

- **Blocked-state event model**: `SagaResumeBlocked` and its checkpoint reducer let the runtime persist manual-intervention state as a durable framework event instead of inferring blocked status indirectly.

- **Pure recovery planning seam**: `SagaRecoveryPlanner<TSaga>` and the shared `SagaStepHash` helper now turn saga state plus checkpoint metadata into deterministic recovery decisions without touching reminder infrastructure yet.

- **Async recovery coordinator seam**: `SagaRecoveryCoordinator<TSaga>` now loads the current saga state from the aggregate grain, loads the latest checkpoint snapshot, and delegates the resulting decision to the planner so later reminder/manual entrypoints can stay thin.

- **Explicit resume command path**: `ResumeSagaCommand`, `ResumeSagaCommandHandler<TSaga>`, and `SagaRecoveryCoordinator<TSaga>.ResumeAsync(...)` now execute actionable recovery plans through the normal aggregate command pipeline instead of introducing a parallel runtime-only path.

- **Replay-only started-event trigger**: `SagaOrchestrationEffect<TSaga>` now executes non-initial `SagaStepExecutionStarted` markers so reminder/manual resumes replay work with durable attempt identity while initial orchestration keeps its existing inline execution semantics.

- **Thin reminder callback seam**: `GenericAggregateGrain<TAggregate>` now implements `IRemindable` and delegates reminder ticks to an optional runtime reminder handler, so saga reminder work stays runtime-owned without forcing non-saga aggregates into saga-specific logic.

- **State-driven reminder reconciliation**: saga orchestration now registers a reminder reconciler that uses persisted checkpoint metadata, runtime options, and Orleans reminder registration APIs to arm, update, or clear the framework recovery reminder whenever saga recovery state changes.

- **Runtime reminder options**: a new `SagaRecoveryOptions` contract now exposes runtime kill switches plus bounded reminder timing/attempt settings, and saga reminder reconciliation clamps overdue or disabled reminders safely.

- **Public recovery service seam**: `ISagaRecoveryService<TSaga>` and `SagaRecoveryService<TSaga>` now provide raw-state reads, metadata-only runtime status, and typed manual resume responses as a stable public/public-facing seam for generated HTTP surfaces.

- **Resource-level saga access**: new access-context and authorizer seams persist caller fingerprints at saga start and enforce fail-closed reads/manual resume, while still permitting legacy unscoped sagas by default.

- **Separate operator runtime status**: generated saga controllers now keep raw `GET status` reads intact while also adding `GET runtime-status` and `POST resume` routes that use the recovery service and typed public contracts.

- **MCP parity over the same seam**: generated saga MCP tools now keep raw state separate while adding `*_runtime_status` and `*_resume` tools that flow through the same recovery service contracts used by HTTP, with read-only vs destructive behavior declared explicitly in MCP metadata.

- **Command-side client scope only**: generated client work adds manual-resume command plumbing and typed response handling without inventing a brand-new runtime-status client query model.

- **Projection-aligned recovery status**: `[GenerateSagaStatusReducers]` now emits reducers for execution-started, blocked-resume, and compensated-step recovery events so projection read models can mirror the framework recovery metadata without handwritten drift.

- **Nullable enum projection compatibility**: client and gateway projection generators now unwrap nullable enums when emitting DTO enums and mapping code, which keeps recovery metadata fields like `PendingDirection` and `LastResumeSource` working in generated projection surfaces.

- **Spring operator sample**: the Spring money-transfer sample now surfaces recovery mode/disposition, pending work, blocked state, last resume metadata, and a typed manual-resume action directly in the operations UI.



### Code Example



```csharp

[SagaRecovery]

[SagaStep<MoneyTransferSagaState>(

    0,

    SagaStepRecoveryPolicy.ManualOnly,

    CompensationRecoveryPolicy = SagaStepRecoveryPolicy.ManualOnly)]

internal sealed class WithdrawFromSourceStep

    : ISagaStep<MoneyTransferSagaState>,

      ICompensatable<MoneyTransferSagaState>

{

    public Task<StepResult> ExecuteAsync(

        MoneyTransferSagaState state,

        SagaStepExecutionContext context,

        CancellationToken cancellationToken)

    {

        // Later increments use context for replay-safe recovery decisions.

        return Task.FromResult(StepResult.Succeeded());

    }

}

```



## Observability



This increment adds reminder-callback debug logs on `GenericAggregateGrain<TAggregate>` for reminder receipt, ignored reminder names, and processed reminder ticks. Metrics, health checks, and reconciliation telemetry remain deferred to later reminder-lifecycle increments.



## Files Changed

| `src/DomainModeling.Abstractions/ISagaRecoveryInfoProvider.cs` | Exposes saga-level recovery metadata to runtime consumers without reflection. |

title: Add ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS config option for Hugging Face repos outside the org
body:
Mirrors the existing `ADDITIONAL_REPOS` (GitHub) pattern for Hugging Face. Each entry specifies the repo ID and its type since HF API endpoints differ by repo type.

### Config format

```yaml
ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS:
  - repo: "user/dataset-name"
    type: "datasets"
  - repo: "user/model-name"
    type: "models"
  - repo: "user/space-name"
    type: "spaces"
```

The parameter is optional — defaults to `[]` when absent from `config.yaml`.

### Changes

- **`main.js`**: In `fetchHubItems()`, after fetching org items for a given HF type, filters `ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS` entries matching that type, deduplicates by `item.id`, and fetches each additional repo via `${API_BASE_URL}${repoType}/${entry.repo}`. Added config validation and module-scope variable.
- **`scripts/export-tags.js`**: Same fetch-and-merge logic so the tag export script picks up tags from additional HF repos.
- **`public/config.yaml`**: New parameter with commented usage examples.
- **`README.md`**: Documented `ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS` alongside `ADDITIONAL_REPOS`.

title: fix: restructure CLAUDE.md from wiki to rulebook
body:
## Summary

Restructure `CLAUDE.md` to enforce global LXC-first container deployment rule and prevent AI sessions from defaulting to Docker for new services. This repo is a Docker exception—not the norm.

## Root Cause

The original `CLAUDE.md` was a wiki-style document with extensive Docker and HEC token tutorials. AI sessions reading this repo's instructions would naturally assume Docker was the canonical container strategy. This information locality failure contradicted the global rule in [nix-ai#420](https://github.com/JacobPEvans/nix-ai/pull/420): **LXC is the default; Docker is justified only for this Splunk exception.**

## Changes

### Main Changes

- **CLAUDE.md**: Reduced from 145 to 71 lines
  - Added "Container Strategy: Docker (Exception)" callout at the top with link to nix-ai#420
  - Replaced environment variable table with concise "Sources of Truth" pointer to Doppler and `.envrc`
  - Moved HEC token derivation tutorial to `roles/splunk_docker/README.md` (operational detail, not architectural)
  - Moved MCP verification steps to `roles/splunk_docker/README.md` (role-specific, not repo-wide)

- **`.claude/rules/nix-tool-execution.md`**: Deleted
  - This rule is now superseded by the global `nix-tool-policy.md` in [nix-ai#420](https://github.com/JacobPEvans/nix-ai/pull/420)
  - Removal signals that this repo follows shared standards

### Auto-Fixes

- **CHANGELOG.md**: Fixed markdownlint violations (blank line spacing)

head: 9b9a04b6a5af7b0f8e7437ca6a2eb58aaf91e428
title: feat: wire live context token counts through engine to compaction guards
body:
## Summary

Wires live observed token counts from the engine layer into the compaction guards added in #306, so headroom and cache-aware skip decisions use fresh data instead of potentially stale stored counts. Also propagates the new config fields (`leafSkipReductionThreshold`, `leafBudgetHeadroomFactor`) from `LcmConfig` into `CompactionConfig`.

**Part 2 of 3 from #289 split. Depends on #306. Merge order: #306 → #307 → #308.**

---

## The Problem: Stale Token Counts Cause Wrong Guard Decisions

The compaction guards in #306 decide whether to skip or compact based on `totalAssembledTokens` — a value derived from the stored token count in the database. But stored counts can lag behind reality:

### Stale-low scenario (most dangerous)

After rapid message ingestion (e.g., a tool that emits 15 messages in 1 second), the DB count hasn't caught up:
- **Stored count**: 30K (stale from 2 seconds ago)
- **Live count**: 75K (actual prompt tokens the API will see)
- **Budget ceiling**: 60K

Without live counts, the headroom guard sees 30K < 60K → **SKIP**. But the context is actually 75K — well over the ceiling. The guard should detect budget pressure and **COMPACT**.

### The fix: `max(stored, live)`

By passing `liveContextTokens` (from `estimateSessionTokenCountForAfterTurn`) through to `evaluateLeafTrigger`, the guard uses whichever count is higher:
- Stale-low stored → uses live (prevents missed compaction)
- Stale-high stored → uses stored (conservative, prevents premature skip)

This is the safe/conservative choice — it errs on the side of compacting when counts disagree, which is the correct bias for preventing context overflow.

---

## What This PR Wires

### Engine → CompactionEngine config

`LcmConfig` now flows `leafSkipReductionThreshold` and `leafBudgetHeadroomFactor` into the `CompactionConfig` object, so plugin/env var overrides actually take effect at runtime (without this, the guards always use their internal defaults).

### afterTurn → evaluateLeafTrigger

The engine's `afterTurn()` already computes `liveContextTokens` — this PR passes it (along with `tokenBudget`) through to `evaluateLeafTrigger()` so the guards can make informed decisions.

### afterTurn logging

New structured logging for compaction decisions:
- **Trigger**: `[lcm] afterTurn: leaf compaction triggered (raw=24000, threshold=20000, assembled=548000, pressure=true)`
- **Skip**: `[lcm] afterTurn: leaf compaction skipped (budget-headroom: 30000 assembled < 120000 ceiling)`

These match the log lines documented in the tuning guide (#308).

### compactLeaf/compactFullSweep → currentTokenCount

Both paths now pass `observedTokens` (from `normalizeObservedTokenCount`) as `currentTokenCount`, which `evaluateLeafTrigger` uses as `precomputedTokenCount` to avoid a duplicate DB read.

### compact() type fix

`compact()` wrapper now includes `currentTokenCount` in its input type so TypeScript excess-property checks pass and the value flows through to `compactFullSweep`.

### LeafTriggerResult import

Engine's `evaluateLeafTrigger` now imports `LeafTriggerResult` from `compaction.ts` instead of re-declaring the shape inline, preventing type drift.

### README env var table

Added `LCM_LEAF_SKIP_REDUCTION_THRESHOLD`, `LCM_LEAF_BUDGET_HEADROOM_FACTOR`, and `LCM_FALLBACK_PROVIDERS` to the README environment variable reference table.

---

## Changes by File

| File | Lines | Change |
|------|-------|--------|
| `src/engine.ts` | +26/-3 | Pass config fields to CompactionConfig. Pass `tokenBudget` + `liveContextTokens` to `evaluateLeafTrigger` from afterTurn. Pass `currentTokenCount` to `compactLeaf`/`compact`. Import `LeafTriggerResult`. Add trigger/skip logging. |
| `src/compaction.ts` | +1 | Add `currentTokenCount` to `compact()` input type. |
| `test/engine.test.ts` | +48/-1 | Update `evaluateLeafTrigger` assertion for 4-arg signature. Add `currentTokenCount` to compact plumbing assertions. New test: `compactLeafAsync` passes `currentTokenCount`. New test: omission when not provided. |
| `test/lcm-integration.test.ts` | +2 | Shrink test message bodies (was 12KB strings, now short descriptive text). |
| `README.md` | +3 | Add 3 env vars to reference table. |

## Test Plan

- [x] 204 tests passing (122 engine + 82 integration)
- [x] `evaluateLeafTrigger` called with `(sessionId, sessionKey, tokenBudget, liveContextTokens)`
- [x] `currentTokenCount: 500` flows through compact plumbing to `compactFullSweep`
- [x] `currentTokenCount` omitted from `compactLeaf` call when not provided (no undefined leakage)
- [x] Stale-token integration tests: compactLeaf and compactFullSweep trigger with live counts

head: 9586cd0abc7db9ca86686e592c2a808f0f26b32f
title: Refactor crawler auth to state-machine session orchestration (deduped login + service handshakes)
body:
### **User description**
Current crawlers share `WebAp` cookies and could race on session creation, causing concurrent relogins and cross-service session interference. This change introduces explicit session state orchestration so auth, invalidation, and retries are coordinated instead of ad-hoc per helper.

- **L1: WebAp session state machine**
  - Added `WebApSessionState` (`idle/authenticating/verifying/authenticated/expired/backoff/failed`).
  - Replaced implicit `isLogin + checkLogin()` flow with `ensureAuthenticated()` single-flight auth (`_loginFuture`) and post-login verification (`_verifyWebApSession()`).
  - Added centralized invalidation path (`markSessionInvalid`) and bounded backoff handling.

- **L2: Service session coordination**
  - Added `WebApServiceSessionState` and `WebApServiceType`.
  - Introduced `_ensureServiceSession(...)` to single-flight handshake per downstream service (`leave/stdsys/mobile/oosaf`).
  - Routed `loginToLeave/loginToStdsys/loginToMobile/loginToOosaf` through this gate to avoid duplicate handshakes under concurrency.

- **Request-path retry semantics**
  - Reworked `apQuery()` from recursive relogin to loop-based retry with explicit state transitions:
    - parser code indicates expired session → mark expired → backoff → re-authenticate.
  - Keeps retry policy centralized and prevents recursive contention patterns.

- **State reset / compatibility**
  - Added `resetSessionMachine()` and wired session cleanup into existing logout/reset flows.
  - Kept `checkLogin()` as deprecated compatibility shim, forwarding to `ensureAuthenticated()`.

```dart
Future<void> ensureAuthenticated() async {
  if (sessionState == WebApSessionState.authenticated && isLogin) return;
  if (_loginFuture != null) {
    await _loginFuture; // dedupe concurrent login callers
    if (sessionState != WebApSessionState.authenticated || !isLogin) {
      throw GeneralResponse(statusCode: ApStatusCode.networkConnectFail);
    }
    return;
  }
  sessionState = WebApSessionState.authenticating;
  _loginFuture = _authenticateWithVerify();
  try { await _loginFuture; } finally { _loginFuture = null; }
}
```


___

### **PR Type**
Bug fix, Enhancement


___

### **Description**
- 重構 WebAp 認證為狀態機。

- 引入單次飛行認證以避免重複登入。

- 為服務會話新增協調機制。

- 實作指數退避和集中式重試。


___

### Diagram Walkthrough


```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[使用者請求] --> B{WebApHelper.apQuery() 或 loginToXxx()}
    B --> C{WebApHelper.ensureAuthenticated()}
    C -- "管理 WebAp 會話狀態" --> D(WebApSessionState)
    B -- "透過 _ensureServiceSession()" --> E{協調服務會話}
    E -- "管理服務會話狀態" --> F(WebApServiceSessionState)
    D -- "會話過期/失敗" --> G[觸發重新認證/退避]
    G --> C
```

head: 2378227172859b977f576fa1a1e3dfd4b52fa524
title: ci: fix grype-remediation-suggestions trigger, run ID resolution, underfixed false-positives, and least-privilege
body:
Five correctness and security issues across the Grype automation workflows, including a condition that silently prevented the remediation-suggestions workflow from ever running automatically.

## `grype-remediation-suggestions.yml`

- **Drop `head_branch` guard** — `workflow_run.head_branch` reflects the branch owning the workflow file (`main`), not the branch checked out internally. The `== 'pre-update-release'` condition always evaluated false for scheduled runs.
- **Fix `workflow_dispatch` run ID fallback** — when `run_id` is omitted, `github.event.workflow_run.id` is empty on `workflow_dispatch` events. Now resolves via API: prefers the most recent successful `Weekly Grype Security Scan` run on `pre-update-release` within the last 7 days, falls back to the absolute latest if none found.
- **Filter PRs from issue search** — `issues.listForRepo` returns both issues and PRs; added `&& !i.pull_request` to prevent accidentally updating a PR body instead of the tracking issue.

## `dependabot-grype-guard.yml`

- **Drop `pull-requests: write`** — the workflow only writes to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and uploads artifacts; issue/PR creation from scan results is handled by `grype-remediation-suggestions.yml`. Only `contents: read` is required.
- **Scope `underfixed_updates` to High/Critical fixable vulns** — the previous logic false-positived when a package had an unrelated unfixable High vuln alongside a Medium fixable vuln. Added `fixed_high_critical_recommendations()` that filters to High/Critical severity before checking fix state; a package is only flagged underfixed if it was changed *and* still carries a fixable High/Critical finding in the PR image.

```python
# Before: any fixable vuln on the package triggered the check
underfixed_updates = [pkg for pkg in changed if pkg in recs and ("High" in severities or "Critical" in severities)]

# After: only packages with High/Critical fixable vulns are considered
high_critical_recs = fixed_high_critical_recommendations(pr)  # scoped to sev ∈ {High, Critical}
underfixed_updates = [pkg for pkg in changed if pkg in high_critical_recs]
```

head: f63a02462d1eebd5b06b45ebdf1d2705c919413a
title: Add non-blocking partition access via PartitionGuard
body:
### Summary
Introduces a PartitionGuard type to the partition-manager crate that provides both async (lock) and non-blocking (try_lock) access to partition storage, along with hardened arithmetic to prevent integer overflow.

## Motivation
When a task panics while holding a partition's mutex, the lock remains held. If the panic handler itself needs to access the same partition (e.g., to persist crash logs or diagnostic data), calling `lock().await` would deadlock. The handler is waiting on a lock that will never be released. By exposing `try_lock()`, callers like panic handlers can attempt non-blocking access and gracefully handle failure instead of deadlocking the system.

## Changes
- Added `PartitionGuard` struct with `lock()` (async) and `try_lock()` (non-blocking) constructors on Partition
- Implemented `BlockDevice`, `ReadNorFlash`, and `NorFlash` traits for PartitionGuard
- Re-exported `TryLockError` from embassy_sync for caller convenience
- Hardened all partition offset/size arithmetic with checked operations to prevent integer overflow
- Added unit tests covering guard-based read/write/erase, out-of-bounds access, overflow edge cases, and lock contention via `try_lock()`

- **Step 4c run conditions** (slice 1): gates on Step 4a having written a marker AND board credentials being present in `.clancy/.env`. Either gate failing → silent skip + continue to Step 7. Step 4b's tail rewritten to route through 4c instead of jumping to Step 7.
- **Source read** (slice 2): reads `**Source:**` directly from `.clancy/plans/{stem}.md`. Single source of truth — does not chase the brief file the way Step 4b does.
- **Three-format parser** (slice 3): bracketed `[KEY] Title` is the only pushable format. Inline-quoted `"text"` and file-path `path/to.md` route to the skip branch with `BOARD_PUSH_SKIPPED_NO_TICKET`.
- **Per-platform key validation** (slice 4): six inline regexes (Jira `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\d+$`, GitHub `^#\d+$`, Linear `^[A-Z]+-\d+$`, Azure DevOps `^\d+$`, Shortcut `^\d+$`, Notion `^[0-9a-f]{32}$\|^[0-9a-f-]{36}$`). Single-board environment, no cross-board disambiguation. Mismatch → hard error with actionable message and exact retry command.
- **Decision matrix** (slice 5): six cells across `--push` × `--afk` × `--ticket`. Two-prompt non-`--afk` flow (Step 4 confirms approval, Step 4c confirms push) is intentional.
- **Drift anchors + byte-equality** (slices 0/6): canonical curl blocks live in `plan.md` Step 5b; an identical duplicate lives in `approve-plan.md` Step 4c between matching anchors. Editing one without updating the other fails the workflow test.
- **Push failure semantics** (slice 7): HTTP non-2xx logs the literal status; transport failure logs the lowercase error class (`network`/`timeout`/`dns`/`auth`). Marker stays, exact retry command printed, never exits non-zero.
- **EEXIST + `--push` retry path** (slice 8): re-running approve-plan with `--push` after a failed push falls through Step 4a's already-approved check, skips Step 4b (brief marker already updated), and re-attempts Step 4c. Original `sha256=` and `approved_at=` preserved. Without `--push`, EEXIST stops as today.
- **Notion flat-text note** (slice 9): conditional informational line in Step 7's local-mode success block when push target is Notion (only Notion — not the other five platforms), so users aren't surprised that markdown styling was flattened by Notion's `rich_text` model.
- **Command file flag docs** (slice 9): `commands/approve-plan.md` documents `--push` and `--ticket KEY` alongside the existing `--afk` from PR 7b.

## Locked spec decisions (recorded in `.claude/plans/plan-package-extraction.md` PR 9 section)

Six decisions locked before slice 0:

1. Push sub-step is **Step 4c**, not "Step 5a" (after 4b, before 7)
2. Retry semantics: **EEXIST + `--push` falls through to 4c** (no new flag, no marker deletion)
3. Source read from **`**Source:**` in the plan file** (not the brief)
4. Comment payload: **full plan content + one-line approval header**
5. Drift-prevention: **HTML comment anchors** (`<!-- curl-blocks:approve-plan-push:start/end -->`)
6. Progress.txt success row: **second row `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN_PUSH | {stem} | {KEY}`** (not extended row)

## Reviews

**Architectural review** (self, after Plan + general-purpose agents both 529'd on Anthropic API capacity):
- COHESION: pass — pushing an approved plan as a board comment is the standalone+board UX cliff fix, symmetric with `/clancy:plan` Step 5b which already pushes plan content to board comments.
- LAYERING: pass — plan stays a leaf, zero new TS runtime deps, no `runPipeline` import, no core/terminal references. Markdown-only diff plus one TS test file in plan.
- SCOPE CREEP: none of substance — the 10 slices map directly onto the 6 locked decisions.

**DA review** (general-purpose agent on retry, after two prior 529s) caught 6 findings, all addressed in `fed52bd`:
- **H1** missing `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN_PUSH` success row (the locked spec mandated it but slice 5 shipped without it) → added to Step 4c success branch
- **H2** stale Step 4a "After writing the marker" prose still said "jump to Step 7" (slice 1 only rewrote Step 4b) → rewrote to "continue to Step 4c"
- **M1** five new PR 9 tokens used `TOKEN | {stem} | {detail}` but the pre-existing `LOCAL_APPROVE_PLAN` row (and `plan.md`'s `LOCAL_PLAN`/`LOCAL_REVISED`) use `{stem} | TOKEN | {detail}` → flipped all five for column-schema consistency
- **M2** the slice 8 EEXIST prose rendered the no-`--push` stop branch first as a full fenced block, with the retry branch buried after it → restructured so the retry branch comes first
- **L1** undocumented BOARD_PUSH_FAILED reason-field disambiguation contract → added explicit prefix-reservation note (HTTP statuses are numeric, error classes are a closed lowercase set, `key-mismatch:` prefix is reserved)
- **L2** slice 1's negative regex only scanned the 4b body slice — the same bug that hid H2 → widened to a regression test that scans the whole 4a→4c span

**Self-review**: 10 commits, clean gitmoji types, all scoped to `(plan)`. Final test count 264. Pre-push suite (`pnpm test && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm format:check && pnpm knip && pnpm publint && pnpm attw`) all green.

- [x] Smoke test: `/clancy:approve-plan {stem} --push` skips the prompt and pushes
- [x] Smoke test: `/clancy:approve-plan {stem} --afk` (no `--push`) stays local-only and logs `LOCAL_ONLY`

title: Add Movie Recorder feature using Unity Recorder
body:
## Summary

- Add recording feature using the Unity Recorder package
- `get_all_recorders` lists all recorder types (Movie, ImageSequence, AnimationClip, etc.) with a `type` field
- Movie Recorder operations (add/remove/start/stop) are scoped under `recorder movie`
- Uses `RecorderControllerSettings.GetGlobalSettings()` to share settings with the Recorder Window

## MCP Tools

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `get_all_recorders` | List all configured recorders with type info |
| `add_movie_recorder` | Add a Movie Recorder |
| `remove_movie_recorder` | Remove a Movie Recorder by index |
| `start_movie_recorder` | Start recording by index |
| `stop_movie_recorder` | Stop recording and return the output path |

## CLI Commands

```
recorder all list
recorder movie add <name> <outputPath> [--encoder] [--encoding-quality]
recorder movie remove <index>
recorder movie start <index> [--fps]
recorder movie stop
```

## API Routes

- `GET /recorder/all/list`
- `POST /recorder/movie/add`
- `POST /recorder/movie/remove`
- `POST /recorder/movie/start`
- `POST /recorder/movie/stop`

## Design Decisions

- `get_all_recorders` returns all recorder types with a `type` field (Movie, ImageSequence, AnimationClip, etc.), while add/remove/start/stop are Movie-specific with type validation
- Indices are global across all recorder types; remove/start validate that the recorder at the given index is a MovieRecorderSettings
- `GetGlobalSettings()` internally calls `LoadSerializedFileAndForget`, creating new deserialized instances on each call. All operations use a single call to avoid instance mismatch
- Output path is retrieved via `OutputFile + "." + EncoderSettings.Extension` to avoid a serialization bug in `BuildAbsolutePath`
- `RecorderFps` is kept generic (no Movie prefix) as FPS is shared across all recorder types
- Encoder type and encoding quality are Movie-specific, hence `MovieRecorderEncoderType` / `MovieRecorderEncodingQuality`

## Test Plan

- [x] Unity Editor tests (225 passed)
- [x] .NET builds (Core, MCP, CLI)
- [x] Core integration tests (69 passed)
- [x] MCP tool verification (`get_all_recorders`, `add/remove/start/stop_movie_recorder`)
- [x] CLI command structure verification (`recorder all list`, `recorder movie add/remove/start/stop`)

## Summary

- **Hook type validation at init**:
    - sync `Throttled` only accepts `Hook`, async `Throttled` only accepts `AsyncHook`.

title: Fix staleness filter for NO variance strategy
body:
## Summary

The staleness filter was removing 77 of 83 eligible markets because their prices hadn't changed in 5 cycles. For a BUY NO variance strategy, stable prices with active volume represent persistent mispricings — the ideal opportunity, not staleness.

Changed the staleness signal from "price unchanged" to "no trading activity": a market is stale only when price is unchanged AND volume is below a floor (default 10) AND open interest hasn't changed. Markets with stable prices but active trading now pass through correctly.

- Replaced `volume_spike_ratio` parameter with `volume_floor` (minimum volume to consider active)
- Added `open_interest` tracking to StalenessEntry for OI-change detection
- Backward compatible with existing `scan_staleness.json` files (old entries missing `open_interest` default to 0)

Closes #467

This pull request introduces a comprehensive set of improvements to the local development environment for the monorepo, focusing on enhanced developer experience, clearer environment configuration, and better support for multi-stack workflows. The main changes include the addition of workspace configurations for frontend, backend, and fullstack development in VS Code, a new environment variables reference file, and updates to the devcontainer for improved service support and automation.

**Key changes:**

#### VS Code Workspace Enhancements

* Added new workspace files: `.vscode/frontend.code-workspace`, `.vscode/backend.code-workspace`, and `.vscode/fullstack.code-workspace` to streamline and standardize frontend, backend, and fullstack development workflows. These files provide pre-configured folders, recommended extensions, launch/debug configurations, and tasks for all major services. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9e98098ec69099e7fafd85bcee505d352258a571a7469ed0b82beaaa1312eedfR1-R147) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-527b28fbedfd2fb7215d8528c5d254c9e41ad6918071b3da15e235c5381eb1fdR1-R136) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-74e37838d5baae0f58f8e366440df828bb59b1e444f9fe99e3873e9571ff8ac6R1-R247)

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bd5430ee7c51dc892a67b3f2829d1f5b6d223f0fd48b82322cfd45baf9f5e945L20-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bd5430ee7c51dc892a67b3f2829d1f5b6d223f0fd48b82322cfd45baf9f5e945L58-R92)

#### Environment Configuration

* Introduced `.env.example` as a centralized reference for all environment variables used across the monorepo, with documentation and guidance for local, Docker, and production setups.

#### Devcontainer Improvements

Also improved the `postStartCommand` to auto-generate files and enhanced VS Code extension recommendations for fullstack development. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-24ad71c8613ddcf6fd23818cb3bb477a1fb6d83af4550b0bad43099813088686R10-R12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-24ad71c8613ddcf6fd23818cb3bb477a1fb6d83af4550b0bad43099813088686R22-R24) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-24ad71c8613ddcf6fd23818cb3bb477a1fb6d83af4550b0bad43099813088686R40-R48) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-24ad71c8613ddcf6fd23818cb3bb477a1fb6d83af4550b0bad43099813088686L47-R62) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-24ad71c8613ddcf6fd23818cb3bb477a1fb6d83af4550b0bad43099813088686R95-R101)

These changes collectively make it much easier to get started with, develop, and debug the monorepo's services in a consistent and efficient manner.

title: Improve geomedian/geomad (0-0-4a), training data, and prediction (0-0-3).
body:
This branch made v0-0-4a of GeoMAD and 0-0-3 of training data, model, and prediction. It was run for the 10 test tiles.

The changes include:
1. Improving Geomedian/GeoMAD creation. Details below.
2. Working process for Pacific, Non-Pacific, and Pacific antimeridian-crossing tiles.
3. I tried to share code between training data creation and prediction.
4. Common geomad/prediction version variables are defined once and used everywhere.
5. Change training data creation process to be per tile, not per country. It still clips tile results to (buffered) country.
6. Improve GeoMAD stac item datetimes.
7. Write/read training data, and model to S3.
8. Speed up get_gadm function using better caching (and make more robust).
9. Visualisation: Match WorldCover colors for classes.



GeoMAD Ideas I am playing with:
- Fix search_kwargs == {} bug — was a comparison, not assignment. Now T1 and T2 data actually load for Pacific LS7 tiles/years.
- Add [qa_radsat](vscode-file://vscode-app/Users/wj/Documents/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) band for masking saturated/occluded pixels. Saturated pixels had extreme values that skewed the geomedian.
- Remove 65535 values in float data as a safety net for any remaining saturated values (uint16 path relies on [qa_radsat](vscode-file://vscode-app/Users/wj/Documents/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) + [nodata=0](vscode-file://vscode-app/Users/wj/Documents/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html)).
- Set [nodata=0](vscode-file://vscode-app/Users/wj/Documents/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) on OdcLoader so the geomedian correctly skips zero-valued pixels instead of treating them as real observations.
- ~~Increase ls7_buffer_years to 2 — searches 5 years instead of 3 for LS7-era tiles, providing more clear observations.~~
- Pass --include-shadow in the Makefile to explicitly mask cloud shadows.
- Set [min_timesteps=10](vscode-file://vscode-app/Users/wj/Documents/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) — at least 10 Landsat scenes must be loaded (before cloud masking) to attempt geomedian.
- ~~Add [min_clear_obs=3](vscode-file://vscode-app/Users/wj/Documents/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) — after geomedian, mask pixels with fewer than 3 clear observations. Removes SLC-off speckle.~~
- Change cloud mask filters to `[("opening", 3), ("dilation", 5), ("erosion", 2)]` and apply morphological filters only to the cloud/shadow mask, not to fill/saturation gaps, to avoid widening SLC-off stripes.

## Summary - Replace the ~350-line regex pipeline (`convertInline`, placeholder extraction/restoration, line-by-line parser) with goldmark configured for Trix editor compatibility via three custom components: `trixTransformer` (tight lists, soft→hard breaks, paragraph spacing), `trixRenderer` (compact blockquotes, HTML escaping, TrixBreak), and `escapedAtParser` (`\@` mention suppression) - Fix `HTMLToMarkdown` round-trip fidelity: blockquote and list handlers now normalize `

Also fix multiline regex matching (`(?i)` → `(?is)`) and trim trailing newlines from code fence content - Promote goldmark from indirect to direct dependency (v1.7.13, already present via glamour) Net: -433/+452 lines across 3 files. Rare in CLI input; CommonMark-correct. - **Setext headings**: `Text\n---` is now an h2 (CommonMark), not paragraph + hr. - **Escaped `%` in URLs**: `\%` produces `%` not `%25` (CommonMark-correct). - **Code blocks**: trailing `\n` inside `` (goldmark standard fenced code output). - **Consecutive lines**: soft line break (`\n`) instead of space join — HTML renders identically. ## Test plan - [x] `bin/ci` green (all checks pass; tidy-check requires committed state) - [x] Existing `TestMarkdownToHTML` / `TestMarkdownToHTMLBackslashEscapes` expectations updated - [x] New tests: `TestMarkdownToHTMLBackslashAtCounts` (4 backslash counts), `TestMarkdownToHTMLMultiParagraphBlockquote` (single/multi/multi-para), `TestMarkdownToHTMLRawHTMLBlock` (single/multiline script), `TestHTMLToMarkdownMultilineBlockquote`, `TestHTMLToMarkdownMultilineParagraph`, `TestHTMLToMarkdownCodeFenceNewline` - [x] `TestEditLoopRoundTrip` with exact assertions: blockquotes (3 variants), lists (plain + continuation), code fences, headings, mixed content - [x] Verify edit loop in `basecamp todos create` / `basecamp messages create` against a real Basecamp account — created todo with heading, bold/italic, list with continuation, multiline blockquote, and code fence; server HTML → markdown → HTML → markdown round-tripped stably with all structure preserved

head: 3a6681c0e9f84cec275f191bb2960d35990f02c1
title: Phase 47: CLI output refactor and workflow bash simplification
body:
## Summary

- Refactor the `output()` API to raw/scalar output by default, with `--json` as opt-in for structured JSON
- Remove `--raw` and `--resolve` flags entirely — raw is the default, inline is unconditional
- Add `--default` flag to config-get, frontmatter get, roadmap get-phase, summary-extract
- Add `--count` flag to staleness-check, `--file` flag for opt-in temp file output
- Add `todo list-by-phase` and `todo scan-phase-linked` subcommands
- Eliminate all AST-triggering bash patterns from workflows (here-strings, @file: unwrap blocks, brace expansion)
- Replace all `2>/dev/null || echo` fallbacks with `--default` flag
- Inject Claude Code AST safety rules into `CLAUDE.md` on install

**Background:** Claude Code's tree-sitter-bash AST safety layer fires independently of sandbox/allowlist settings. No config suppresses it. The only mitigation is writing AST-safe commands and modernizing the CLI output API so workflows don't need workaround patterns.

## Output API refactor

The `output()` function signature changed from `output(result, raw, rawValue)` to `output(result, displayValue)`:

| Scenario | Old | New |
|----------|-----|-----|
| Scalar command | `output(val, raw, String(val))` | `output(val)` |
| Structured command | `output(obj, raw)` | `output(obj)` — auto-detects object, emits JSON |
| Dual command | `output({slug: v}, raw, v)` | `output({slug: v}, v)` — displays `v` by default |
| JSON needed | `--raw` absent | `--json` flag |

- `--raw` removed entirely (was needed on 100% of callers — sign the default was wrong)
- `--json` added as opt-in for JSON-wrapped output
- `--pick` auto-activates JSON mode for field extraction
- `--resolve` removed — inline output is unconditional (50KB @file: threshold gone)
- `--file` added as opt-in for legacy @file: temp file mechanism

## CLI additions

- `staleness-check --count` — numeric-only output, no JSON parsing needed
- `config-get --default <value>` — CLI-level default instead of shell `2>/dev/null || echo`
- `frontmatter get --default`, `roadmap get-phase --default`, `summary-extract --default`
- `todo list-by-phase <N>` and `todo scan-phase-linked <N>`
- AST safety rules injected into `CLAUDE.md` on `gsd install --runtime claude` (skipped for Copilot)

## Workflow cleanup

- All `<<<` here-strings replaced with `echo | ` pipes
- All `[[ "$VAR" == @file:* ]]` unwrap blocks removed (no longer needed)
- All `2>/dev/null || echo` gsd-tools fallbacks replaced with `--default`
- All `--raw` references removed from workflows, agents, commands
- AST safety reference table added to `agent-shared-context.md`
- AST safety block extracted to `templates/ast-safety-rules.md`

## Test Plan

- [x] 1372 tests pass, 0 failures (81 files changed)
- [x] `output(result, displayValue)` emits scalar by default, JSON for objects
- [x] `--json` flag forces JSON output
- [x] `--pick` auto-activates JSON mode
- [x] `--file` produces @file: temp file output
- [x] `--file --pick` extracts field from temp file correctly
- [x] `--default` returns default value on missing data
- [x] `staleness-check --count` returns integer
- [x] `todo list-by-phase` and `todo scan-phase-linked` work
- [x] CLAUDE.md injection: create, append, idempotency, Copilot-skip
- [x] Zero `--raw`, `--resolve`, `<<<`, `@file:*` unwrap patterns remain in source

head: 75909ed2ba1bb034630edf49b18fb58ff5b64c04
title: Suggest and install official extensions for unknown commands
body:
## Summary

When a user runs a command that matches a known official extension that is not installed (e.g. `gh stack`), the CLI offers to install it instead of showing the generic "unknown command" error.

Hidden stub commands are registered for each official extension in the registry. When invoked:

- **Interactive (TTY):** prompts to install with a progress indicator
- **Non-interactive:** prints the `gh extension install` command

Stubs are registered after real extensions and aliases, so installed extensions always take priority.

## Motivation

Reduces friction for installing official extensions.

## Design decisions

- **Hard-coded registry** in `pkg/extensions/official.go`. Teams add extensions via PR. No API calls, no latency.
- **Stub commands** in `pkg/cmd/root/official_extension_stub.go`. Registered as hidden Cobra commands with `DisableFlagParsing` so any user-provided flags do not cause validation errors.
- **Install only.** After installation the user re-runs their command themselves. Keeps the flow simple.
- **Explicit `github.com/` host prefix** in install suggestions so GHES users install from the right place.

## Current official extensions

- `github/gh-aw`
- `github/gh-stack`

head: abcb5d9f237f7428064d3529cc0d7bc822a79424
title: Fix/139 remove base url tool param
body:
1. Removed `baseUrl` invocation parameter from all tool definitions. Now the any API endpoint URLs must be provided through environment variable configuration prior to MCP server startup. Now `baseUrl` is only mentioned in `src/client-manager.ts`, and no longer in any tool implementation file.
2. Made `BaseToolHandler.getRequiredEnvVars()` return a readonly array of `EnvVar`, since the result is only ever read from.
3. Made `BaseToolHandler.getRequiredEnvVars()` an abstract method since all tools override it. This method will probably be further changed as we migrate to YAML configuration, but is a step in sanitizing the existing codebase. 
4. Began making explicitly named `readonly EnvVar` arrays defining common groupings of `EnvVar`s and respelling the per-tool implementations of `getRequiredEnvVars()` to reference. This transformation is not complete, however. Was driven primarily by the tools which now gained new required env var dependencies in the wake of `baseUrl` being removed as a parameter. In the prior codebase, however, those same tools, though, would have still raised an Error had the corresponding env var not been set and the tool also not being invoked with a `baseUrl`. Now those tools will simply not be enabled/available if their dependent URL environment variable is not set at launch time.

After doing this, the whole concept of 'getRequiredEnvVars()` needs to go away in favor of something better / more flexible, like _asking_ the tool if it should be enabled, passing it the configuration or whatnot. But that's not this PR's primary concern. Stopping the illness of URLs provided at tool invocation time is this PR.

Closes #139

head: 009f41901ee1a943ce85425652bc454fe85d2278
title: Fix .Update() marking AfterSaveBehavior.Throw properties as modified via DetectChanges
body:
Fixes #38105

`DbContext.Update()` on an entity with a nullable complex type + discriminator throws during `SaveChanges`:

```
InvalidOperationException: The property 'X.Discriminator' is defined as read-only
after it has been saved, but its value has been modified or marked as modified.
```

Regression from #37394: the snapshot factory stores default values for shadow properties on complex types, so `DetectChanges` finds a false mismatch between the current discriminator value (set by value generator) and the snapshot (null), re-marking the `Throw` property as modified after `SetEntityState` correctly unflagged it.

### Changes

- **`InternalEntryBase.SetEntityState`**: In the `modifyProperties` block, after unflagging `Throw` properties, set their original values to match current values (guarded by `!IsConceptualNull(property)`) inline in the same loop so `DetectChanges` won't find a false mismatch and re-mark them as modified.

- **Test**: Added `Update_entity_with_nullable_complex_type_and_discriminator_does_not_throw` — inserts entity with nullable complex type + discriminator, clears tracker, calls `Update()` with a new disconnected instance, asserts `SaveChangesAsync` succeeds.

A more targeted fix is proposed in #38111, but I believe this is a more robust approach
