head: 9afc1db1dfa755747eea72b33d004ae95c4cced9
title: feat(python): add clear_cancel() to Bash and BashTool
body:
## Summary

- `cancel()` sets a sticky `AtomicBool` that persists across `execute()` calls. Callers that cancel in-flight execution currently have no way to reset the flag without calling `reset()`, which destroys VFS state.
- Add `clear_cancel()` to both `Bash` and `BashTool` Python classes so callers can clear the flag after awaiting the cancelled task, preserving the VFS for subsequent executions in the same session.

## Motivation

When embedding bashkit in a long-lived session where multiple code executions share a single `Bash` instance (to preserve VFS state), calling `cancel()` to abort a stuck execution permanently poisons the instance — every subsequent `execute()` immediately returns `"execution cancelled"`. The only recovery today is `reset()`, which rebuilds the interpreter and loses all VFS state. `clear_cancel()` gives callers a lightweight way to restore the instance to a usable state after a cancellation.

## Changes

- **`crates/bashkit-python/src/lib.rs`**: Add `clear_cancel()` method to both `PyBash` and `PyBashTool` — mirrors `cancel()` but stores `false` instead of `true`. Docstrings include a safety note covering both async and sync callers.
- **`crates/bashkit-python/bashkit/_bashkit.pyi`**: Add `clear_cancel()` type stubs for both `Bash` and `BashTool` with full docstrings.
- **`crates/bashkit-python/README.md`**: Updated Cancellation section to document `clear_cancel()` and clarify when to use it vs `reset()`. Added `clear_cancel()` to the API reference for both `Bash` and `BashTool`.
- **`crates/bashkit-python/tests/_bashkit_categories.py`**: Eight new tests:
  - `test_bash_clear_cancel_allows_subsequent_execution` / `test_bashtool_clear_cancel_allows_subsequent_execution` — sync: cancel → clear_cancel → execute works.
  - `test_bash_async_clear_cancel_after_cancelled_execute` / `test_bashtool_async_clear_cancel_after_cancelled_execute` — async: cancel → await execute → clear_cancel → execute works (the intended recovery flow).
  - `test_bash_clear_cancel_on_fresh_instance_is_noop` / `test_bashtool_clear_cancel_on_fresh_instance_is_noop` — clear_cancel on a never-cancelled instance is harmless.
  - `test_bash_clear_cancel_after_reset_is_noop` / `test_bashtool_clear_cancel_after_reset_is_noop` — cancel → reset → clear_cancel is a safe no-op.
- **`crates/bashkit-python/tests/test_basic.py`**: Added all 8 new test names to `_NAMES` tuple for pytest discovery.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — pass
- [x] `cargo clippy -p bashkit-python` — no warnings (9 pre-existing dead-code warnings in core crate, unrelated)
- [x] `cargo test --test cancellation_tests -p bashkit` — 5/5 pass
- [x] `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` on `crates/bashkit-python` — pass
- [x] `pytest tests/` — 546 passed, 0 failed (includes 8 new `clear_cancel` tests — sync and async — all discovered via `test_basic.py`)

head: 4f18d31b70f5c23aa4a23701ca4cfd85c7eeae25
title: Fix CallToolResult handling across all SDKs
body:
## Problem

When a tool handler returns an MCP `CallToolResult` object (`{ content: [{type, text/data/resource}], isError?: boolean }`), all four SDKs JSON-serialize it and send the raw JSON string over RPC. The LLM then sees `'{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"actual result"}]}'` instead of the actual tool output.

Fixes #937

## Approach

Each SDK's tool result normalization path now detects the `CallToolResult` shape **before** the JSON-serialize fallback and converts it to the SDK's native `ToolResultObject` format:

- **Text** content blocks → `textResultForLlm` (multiple blocks joined with `\n`)
- **Image** content blocks → `binaryResultsForLlm` with `type: "image"`
- **Resource** content blocks → text goes to `textResultForLlm`, blob goes to `binaryResultsForLlm`
- `isError: true` → `resultType: "failure"`

The .NET SDK additionally handles **Microsoft.Extensions.AI** content types (`TextContent`, `DataContent`, and unknown `AIContent` subtypes via `AIJsonUtilities` serialization), since the MCP C# SDK's `McpClientTool` returns these types from `InvokeCoreAsync`.

## Changes by SDK

**Node.js** (`nodejs/src/types.ts`, `session.ts`, `client.ts`)
- `isCallToolResult()` type guard + `convertCallToolResult()` converter
- Integrated into both `_executeToolAndRespond` (session API) and `normalizeToolResultV2` (client API)
- Defensive guards for malformed input (optional chaining on resource, typeof check on text)

**Python** (`python/copilot/tools.py`)
- `_is_call_tool_result()` + `_convert_call_tool_result()` (private helpers)
- Integrated into `_normalize_result`

**Go** (`go/definetool.go`)
- `convertCallToolResult()` with JSON marshal/unmarshal fallback for typed Go structs
- Integrated into `normalizeResult`

**.NET** (`dotnet/src/Types.cs`, `Session.cs`, `Client.cs`)
- `ToolResultObject.TryConvertFromCallToolResult(object?)` — detects `JsonElement` with CallToolResult shape
- `ToolResultObject.TryConvertFromAIContent(object?)` — handles `TextContent`, `DataContent`, `IEnumerable<AIContent>`, with fallback serialization for unknown subtypes
- Integrated into both `ExecuteToolAndRespondAsync` (session) and client v2 tool response path

## Tests

- **Node.js**: 21 unit tests in `nodejs/test/call-tool-result.test.ts`
- **Go**: 9 subtests in `TestConvertCallToolResult`
- **Python**: 13 tests in `TestCallToolResult` class
- Coverage includes: text-only, multiple text, isError mapping, image content, resource text/blob, mixed content, empty content, malformed input rejection, and edge cases

## Summary
Extends the chart `Legend` with optional **label**, **size** (`sm` | `md` | `lg` | `xl`), and **orientation** (`horizontal` | `vertical`). The root now wraps the list in a column layout with `display: inline-flex`, scales label text and swatches via CSS using `data-size`, and **extends `FlexProps`** so consumers (and built-in charts) can control alignment—e.g. `alignSelf="center"` to keep legends centered when the default is no longer `justify-content: center` on the list.
## Why
- Support vertical stacking of legend items when horizontal space is tight.
- Support typography/swatch scaling for different chart densities.
- Optional visible heading that doubles as the list’s accessible name when `label` is set; otherwise behavior falls back to `aria-label="Chart legend"`.
- Charts need explicit centering after the legend’s internal layout change.
## Changes
- **`Legend` API**: `label?`, `size?` (default `md`), `orientation?` (default `horizontal`); inherits omitted `FlexProps<'div'>` (minus `children`) for the root.
- **Structure**: Outer root `Flex` + optional label + inner `role="list"` with row/column direction and spacing tuned per orientation.
- **Styles**: `.root`, `.label`, size variants on `data-size`, swatch dimensions tied to legend font size tokens.
- **Bar chart / line chart**: Pass `alignSelf="center"` for top/bottom legends so placement matches prior centered appearance.
- **Design tokens**: `@property --_fs-base` syntax updated from `<length>` to `*` in `variables.css` (broader compatibility with token usage).

## What changed

- Legacy (tests/bench/): Built on Benchmark.js, Grunt tasks, and CommonJS. Required four extra devDependencies (benchmark, dustjs-linkedin, mustache, underscore) and a custom Grunt task runner (tasks/metrics.js).
- New (bench/): Built on tinybench, ESM modules, with markdown report generation and a comparison/diffing tool.

## Benefits

- Better statistics: tinybench provides p50/p75/p99 latency, relative margin of error, and configurable warmup - Benchmark.js only reported ops/sec with a confidence interval.

Neither dustjs nor mustache are supported anymore, so I removed benchmarks for them, but if you believe they are still useful, I can restore them.

title: fix: verify wrapper-backed runtime binaries via direct exec
body:
## What changed - replace the in-container manifest probe shell in `scripts/verify.sh` with per-entry verification driven by the checked-out runtime manifest - keep shell-based smoke checks for normal binaries - execute wrapper-backed binaries, currently `gemini`, via direct `docker exec ...args` so verify matches the direct-exec path that works in staging ## Why - staging deploy `24170400181` was healthy, but `verify.yml` run `24170520305` still failed on `failed_smoke:gemini:/opt/daisy/bin/gemini --version` - live staging proved the wrapper works when executed directly with `docker exec daisy-openclaw-gateway-1 /opt/daisy/bin/gemini --version` - the failing path was verifier shell mediation, not image provisioning ## Affected files - `scripts/verify.sh` ## Risks / blast radius - limited to runtime verification behavior - wrapper-backed entries now bypass the in-container shell during smoke checks; non-wrapper binaries still use the existing shell path ## Verification performed - `bash -n scripts/verify.sh` - `git diff --check` - live staging evidence: - `docker exec daisy-openclaw-gateway-1 /opt/daisy/bin/gemini --version` succeeds - prior `verify.yml` failure only occurred through the shell-probe path ## Remaining unverified - PR CI after this verifier-only change - post-merge staging verify rerun ## Deployment / rollback impact - requires normal merge -> Docker Release -> staging dry-run -> staging deploy -> verify sequence - rollback is the prior merged verifier behavior if this path regresses ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Chores** * Standardized and consolidated runtime-binary verification into reusable probe routines. * Detects target architecture reliably and selects repo-side runtime manifests accordingly. * Distinguishes wrapper vs non-wrapper binaries to perform appropriate existence and smoke checks, recording resolved paths. * Improved error handling and clearer diagnostics for missing or failing runtime checks.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; the fix is well-scoped and matches the verified staging execution path. The core change is correct: replacing the shell-mediated probe with direct docker exec for wrapper-backed binaries matches the live staging evidence. All inputs are properly quoted via printf '%q', and the complexity guard prevents shell-metacharacter injection before any remote execution. The one comment left is a P2 duplication nit that does not affect correctness. Non-wrapper binaries are unchanged. No files require special attention.

Vulnerabilities

 No security concerns identified. User-controlled inputs (binary paths, smoke suffixes) are passed through `printf '%q'` quoting before being embedded in remote commands. The smoke-suffix complexity guard explicitly rejects shell metacharacters (`'`, `"`, `\`, `|`, `>`, `<`, `;`, `&`) before any remote execution. Credentials and host paths are validated against allow-list patterns before use.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | scripts/verify.sh | Core verification script refactored to use direct docker exec for wrapper-backed binaries; logic is sound with minor code-duplication between the container and image branches of build_target_direct_exec_command. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[verify_runtime_binaries_for_target] --> B[Check manifest exists in target] B --> C[Detect target arch via dpkg] C --> D[Load manifest entries for arch from repo] D --> E{For each entry} E --> F{wrapper_type == node-entrypoint?} F -- Yes --> G[build_target_wrapper_test_command\ncheck -x binary_path] G --> H[gce_ssh: test -x /opt/daisy/bin/binary] H --> I[build_target_direct_exec_command] I -- container --> J[sudo docker exec container binary args] I -- image --> K[sudo docker run --rm --entrypoint binary image args] J --> L[gce_ssh smoke: output discarded] K --> L L --> M[append_runtime_bin_line binary binary_path] F -- No --> N[Build shell probe\ncommand -v + smoke_command] N --> O[gce_ssh: sh -c probe] O --> P[append_runtime_bin_line binary resolved_path] M --> E P --> E E --> Q[printf runtime_bins] ```

Comments Outside Diff (1)

 1. `scripts/verify.sh`, line 444-447 ([link](https://github.com/hughdidit/daisy-agency/blob/1b1dee6d1bac6a4716673e79f2e871d72effcee1/scripts/verify.sh#L444-L447)) **Unbound variable `runtime_binary_probe_escaped` breaks sandbox smoke check** `runtime_binary_probe_escaped` is referenced here but is never assigned anywhere in the script. Under `set -euo pipefail`, the `-u` flag causes bash to abort with a "parameter not set" error the moment this line is reached — so Check 8 will hard-fail (not just return a bad exit code) whenever `sandbox_enabled == "true"`. The old Check 3 logic appears to have built a probe script and stored it in this variable, which the sandbox check then reused. This PR switched Check 3 to per-entry iteration from the repo manifest (lines 177-214) but left this reference intact without providing a replacement probe for the sandbox image. The sandbox image (`docker run --rm ...`) can't use the same per-entry `docker exec` path, so it needs its own solution — for example re-using the non-wrapper shell probe loop or a purpose-built probe command for the sandbox image.

head: 06f9d050aef8ca40c6c1a49478aecee995dce362
title: Prevent YAML billion-laughs attacks by rejecting anchors/aliases
body:
## Summary
Prevent YAML billion-laughs denial-of-service attacks by rejecting anchor/alias syntax before unmarshalling.

## Key Changes
- **`internal/lint/yamlsafe.go`**: `RejectYAMLAliases()` decodes YAML into a `yaml.Node` tree (which does not expand aliases) and walks it to detect anchors or alias nodes. Also catches undefined alias parse errors.
- **Guard all 11 `yaml.Unmarshal` call sites** with a `RejectYAMLAliases()` check before unmarshalling
- **Comprehensive test coverage** across all packages: unit tests, integration tests, and e2e tests exercising the rejection path at each call site
- **`readDocFrontMatterRaw`** now surfaces diagnostics for both anchor/alias rejection and YAML parse errors instead of silently returning nil

## Implementation Details
- Uses `yaml.NewDecoder` + `yaml.Node` tree walk — safe because `yaml.Node` preserves `AliasNode` without expansion
- Undefined aliases (parse error with "unknown anchor") are also caught
- Error messages are lowercase per repo convention
- Legitimate `&`/`*` in string values, block scalars, and comments are correctly accepted

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests for anchors, aliases, quoted strings, block scalars, comments, escaped quotes, syntax errors, multi-document YAML
- [x] Integration test: front matter with anchors is rejected, clean front matter with Q&A is accepted
- [x] Tests at each call site: config.Load, yamlHasKey, ParseYAMLBody, readFrontMatter, readDocFrontMatterRaw, deriveFrontMatterCUE, extractRequireDirective, parseSchemaFrontMatter, LoadConfig, mergeLocalOverrides, query subcommand
- [x] All CI checks pass including codecov

head: 8be727e43f0bfd1dd285794ce5c557b5ea44336e
title: Size and lay out class diagram nodes from compartment content
body:
Class diagram nodes were sized only from their primary label, causing compartment text (attributes, methods, stereotypes) to clip or overflow the rendered box.

## Layout engine (`DefaultLayoutEngine.cs`)

- Added `SizeClassNode`: width = widest content across class name, annotations, and all compartment lines + 2×padding; height = header section + per-compartment sections (divider + compact padding + lines)
- `SizeStandardNode` delegates to `SizeClassNode` when `node.Compartments.Count > 0`; all non-compartment nodes are unaffected
- Stores `label:centerY` (class name center within header, not full-node center) and `class:headerHeight` in `Node.Metadata` for renderer use
- Directional BFS layer layout is fully preserved — no new graph algorithm introduced

## Renderer (`SvgNodeWriter.cs`)

- Added `AppendClassCompartments`, called from `AppendNode` when compartments or annotations are present
- Renders annotations centered above the class name in the header
- Draws full-width `<line>` dividers at `class:headerHeight` and between compartments using `baseStroke`/`theme.StrokeWidth`
- Renders compartment lines left-aligned at `NodePadding` from the left edge

```
┌──────────────────────┐
│    <<entity>>        │  ← annotation (centered)
│      Order           │  ← class name at label:centerY
├──────────────────────┤  ← divider at class:headerHeight
│ +id: Guid            │  ← left-aligned, compPad top/bottom
│ +status: string      │
├──────────────────────┤
│ +submit(): void      │
└──────────────────────┘
```

## Tests (`ClassDiagramLayoutTests.cs`, new)

head: 7d62e090c20e28e78685700094b2440e7f576711
title: refactor: normalize repo result model with subResults array
body:
## Normalize repo result model

Each feature operation now produces a normalized sub-result:
```js
{ kind: 'code-scanning', status: 'changed' | 'warning', message: '...',
  syncStatus?: 'pr-up-to-date', prNumber?: 42, prUrl?: '...' }
```

Only reportable items are included — unchanged/skipped operations do not push sub-results.

This replaces the fragile property-name enumeration with a single `subResults` array that all consumers iterate:
- `hasRepositoryChanges()` → `subResults.some(s => s.status === 'changed')`
- `hasWarnings` → derived from `subResults.some(s => s.status === 'warning')`
- Summary details → `subResults.filter(changed|warning).map(formatSubResultSummary).join('; ')`

### What changed
- Added `SubResultStatus` enum and `createSubResult()` helper
- Each feature in `updateRepositorySettings` and each sync helper in `run()` pushes a sub-result
- Removed `getChangesList()` (270 lines of property enumeration)
- Removed `warningKeys` Set dedup filter — each feature pushes exactly one sub-result, so duplicates are impossible
- Simplified `hasRepositoryChanges()` to a one-liner
- Legacy properties preserved on the result object for backward compat of the `results` JSON output (marked with `TODO(v3)` for future cleanup)
- Added `SYNC_KIND_LABELS` map and `formatSubResultSummary()` for curated summary table labels (e.g., "PR template" instead of raw file paths) and "pending merge" phrasing
- Added `formatPrLink()` with URL sanitization (protocol validation, HTML attribute escaping) for clickable PR links in summary table
- Added direct unit tests for `escapeHtmlAttribute` and `formatPrLink`

### Behavior change
Warning-only repos no longer count as `changed-repositories` since no change actually succeeded. Repos with both changes and warnings still count as changed.

### References
- Closes #118
- Includes #122 (PR link rendering + URL sanitization)
- Inspired by [CCR feedback](https://github.com/joshjohanning/bulk-github-repo-settings-sync-action/pull/116#discussion_r3012944737) on PR #116

head: a9fce75678bb88cbbaabf793b8e7bd89abc100fb
title: fix: resolve false-positive file detection by switching to GitHub API
body:
Closes #95

## Summary

Fix false-positive file detection when a PR branch includes commits from previously-merged PRs, by switching from git CLI to GitHub API for all file and content operations.

## Background

When a PR branch carries commits from a previously-merged PR, the action was incorrectly flagging files that had no net diff. For example, if `src/index.js` was changed in a prior merged PR, that commit still appeared in `pulls.listCommits` even though `src/index.js` had no diff in the current PR. See #95 for the full scenario.

## Changes

**File detection:**
- Use `pulls.listFiles` (PR diff) as source of truth instead of `git diff`
- Commit analysis (`applySkipKeywordFilter`) only runs when PR diff has relevant files AND a commit matches the skip keyword

**File content retrieval:**
- Replace `git show` with `repos.getContent` API for reading package.json, package-lock.json, and action.yml at specific refs
- Remove `execGit`, `sanitizeFilePath`, `SAFE_GIT_COMMANDS/OPTIONS`, and the `@actions/exec` dependency from runtime

**Token handling:**
- Token is now required (was already effectively required for tag fetching)
- Fail early with clear error if no token provided
- Remove dead no-token git-diff fallback code

**GHES/GHEC-DR:**
- All `getOctokit` calls use `process.env.GITHUB_API_URL` (automatically set by the Actions runner) for enterprise compatibility

**API call optimization by scenario:**
- No relevant files in PR diff: 1 call (listFiles) → skip
- Relevant files, no keyword match: 2 calls (listFiles + listCommits)
- Relevant files, keyword match: 2 + N calls (per non-skipped commit)
- `skip-version-keyword=''`: 1 call (listFiles only)

head: 3bb1ca09fd515c03d77e168e48ba347734b2ef16
title: feat(memory): redesign memory system with tool-based capture and structured storage
body:
## Summary

Complete redesign of the memory system. Replaces broken regex-based capture with an intelligent tool-based approach where the AI itself decides what's worth remembering.

**Before**: 3 overly-broad regex patterns matched random substrings of user prompts, producing garbage "preferences" with no semantic value.

**After**: Three new tools (`oc_memory_save`, `oc_memory_search`, `oc_memory_forget`) let the AI save structured memories with kind, scope, confidence, reasoning, and tags. Memories are deduplicated via Jaccard bigram overlap and reinforced with evidence tracking.

## What Changed

### New Files (12)
- `src/memory/dedup.ts` — Jaccard bigram dedup pipeline with merge-on-match
- `src/memory/memories.ts` — Memory CRUD (save/search/get/forget) with FTS5 + BM25
- `src/tools/memory-save.ts` — `oc_memory_save` tool registration
- `src/tools/memory-search.ts` — `oc_memory_search` tool registration
- `src/tools/memory-forget.ts` — `oc_memory_forget` tool registration
- `tests/memory/dedup.test.ts` — 15 dedup tests
- `tests/memory/memories.test.ts` — 7 CRUD tests
- `tests/tools/memory-save.test.ts` — Save tool tests
- `tests/tools/memory-search.test.ts` — Search tool tests
- `tests/tools/memory-forget.test.ts` — Forget tool tests

### Modified Files (16)
- `src/memory/constants.ts` — V2 constants (kinds, scopes, statuses, weights, thresholds)
- `src/memory/schemas.ts` — V2 Zod schemas for structured memories
- `src/memory/types.ts` — V2 TypeScript types
- `src/memory/database.ts` — `memories`, `memory_evidence`, `memories_fts` tables
- `src/memory/retrieval.ts` — V2 retrieval groups by kind (mistakes > workflow_rules > decisions > preferences > project_facts), token-budgeted
- `src/memory/injector.ts` — Auto-switches to V2 when memories table has active records, falls back to V1
- `src/memory/capture-utils.ts` — Removed all regex patterns, kept only `extractSessionId` and `truncate`
- `src/memory/capture.ts` — Chat handler is now a no-op (tools replace passive capture)
- `src/memory/index.ts` — V2 exports
- `src/index.ts` — Registers 3 new tools, adds one-time migration on load
- `src/inspect/repository.ts` — Extended overview with V2 stats
- `src/tools/memory-status.ts` — Updated interface for V2
- `tests/memory/retrieval.test.ts` — 10 V2 retrieval tests
- `tests/memory/injector.test.ts` — 3 V2 injector + 3 cache invalidation tests
- `tests/memory/capture.test.ts` — Replaced regex tests with no-op handler tests
- `tests/index.test.ts` — Updated expected tool count (34 → 37)

## Architecture

### Memory Schema
5 memory kinds: `preference | decision | project_fact | mistake | workflow_rule`
2 scopes: `project | user`
3 statuses: `active | superseded | rejected`

### Deduplication
- Bigram Jaccard overlap with configurable threshold (0.6)
- Duplicate → merge evidence, bump confidence, update content
- Near-miss → save as new memory

### Retrieval Priority
Memories injected into system prompt ordered by importance:
`mistake > workflow_rule > decision > preference > project_fact`

### Migration
Existing V1 preferences are migrated to V2 memories on first load (one-time, best-effort). Legacy tables preserved for backward compat.

## Verification
- **2235 tests pass** (11 failures are pre-existing supermemory/ research repo, unrelated)
- **Biome lint clean** on all 17 changed files
- **Zero LSP type errors** across all changed files
- 26 files changed, +2651 / -275 lines

2. `4ce7ce3` feat(memory): implement dedup pipeline and memory CRUD repository
3. `c9b028f` feat(memory): add oc_memory_save, oc_memory_search, oc_memory_forget tools
4. `ae69b42` feat(memory): rewrite retrieval and injector to use memories table
5. `764f12a` refactor(memory): remove regex capture, neutralize chat handler
6. `9300679` feat(memory): wire V2 tools, add migration, update memory status

head: 9f34384dd77b616bb25db01a40e2acb667d95c16
title: Chore/update lez
body:
Closes #43
Closes #48

## Summary

This PR updates LEZ to `v0.2.0-rc1` and SPEL to `v0.2.0-rc2`.  That also required updating the direct SPEL dependencies to the current RC line, because the guest entrypoints and IDL tooling in this repo consume the LEZ runtime through `spel-framework`.

It also started to use `tag` instead of `rev` because SPEL is using `tag`, but the Cargo.lock is a tracked file, and as it carries the exact commit hash, the safety result ends up being identical. 

The main LEZ changes that matter here are the new public-claim rules, plus the new `self_program_id` and `caller_program_id` plumbing. The Token, AMM, and ATA changes in this PR were chosen to keep the existing programs stable under those upstream rules, and the implementation follows the decisions discussed in LEZ PRs.

Upstream context the changes are within the main LEZ discussion in:

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/logos-execution-zone/pull/414

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/logos-execution-zone/pull/426

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/logos-execution-zone/pull/428

## Justification

LEZ changed how public accounts can be claimed. A public account can now only be claimed if the call proves authorization for that account or proves a PDA seed for it. That affects how Token creates new public holdings, how AMM creates the first LP holding for a user, and how ATA transfers into a fresh recipient ATA.

The LEZ update also changed the runtime input shape through `self_program_id` and `caller_program_id`. Those changes are mostly absorbed through the dependency update, but they are part of why LEZ and SPEL had to move together in this PR.

## Important contract changes

- Token public mint and transfer no longer assume that a raw public recipient can always be created on the fly. A fresh public recipient now needs explicit authorization in the same transaction.
- `AMM::NewDefinition` now requires `user_lp` authorization when the LP holding is being created for the first time.
- `ATA::Transfer` is now explicitly ATA-to-ATA and takes `(owner, sender_ata, recipient_owner, recipient_ata)`.

## Commit-by-commit changes

### `b1a5afb` refactor!: Update dependencies and implement new required features across multiple modules

This is the base compatibility commit. It aligns direct LEZ pins to `v0.2.0-rc1`, aligns direct SPEL pins to `v0.2.0-rc.2`, refreshes the lockfiles, and updates the claim and post-state handling needed by the LEZ bump across Token, AMM, and ATA. This is a breaking compatibility change because it updates the runtime contract used by all three programs.

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/lez-programs/blob/90ca372de4ca829623712fa86c540924ed1b53cc/Cargo.toml#L22-L24

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/lez-programs/blob/90ca372de4ca829623712fa86c540924ed1b53cc/token/methods/guest/Cargo.toml#L12-L19

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/lez-programs/blob/90ca372de4ca829623712fa86c540924ed1b53cc/ata/src/create.rs#L6-L46

### `5ecdd62` test(token): cover fresh public recipient authorization

This commit does not change token behavior. It makes the new public-recipient contract explicit in docs and integration tests, so the suite now shows that the old raw public auto-create flow is no longer assumed, while a fresh public recipient still works if that recipient explicitly authorizes the transaction.

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/lez-programs/blob/90ca372de4ca829623712fa86c540924ed1b53cc/token/core/src/lib.rs#L10-L16

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/lez-programs/blob/90ca372de4ca829623712fa86c540924ed1b53cc/integration_tests/tests/token.rs#L218-L479

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/logos-execution-zone/pull/414

### `b8d3d2f` fix(amm)!: require auth for fresh user lp holding

This is a breaking client-contract change. First-time pool creation still works in one transaction, but only if `user_lp` is authorized when the LP holding starts from the default state, which keeps the original UX alive under the new LEZ claim rules instead of forcing a silent pre-create step.

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/lez-programs/blob/90ca372de4ca829623712fa86c540924ed1b53cc/amm/src/new_definition.rs#L76-L85

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/lez-programs/blob/90ca372de4ca829623712fa86c540924ed1b53cc/integration_tests/tests/amm.rs#L939-L1204

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/logos-execution-zone/pull/414

### `5c7e6bb` fix(ata)!: require recipient ata for transfers

This is a breaking ATA API change, but it preserves the higher-level ATA UX. Transfers to a fresh recipient ATA work again because ATA now receives the recipient owner, derives the recipient PDA itself, and authorizes the downstream token call correctly. The API is now ATA-to-ATA, not ATA-to-arbitrary-holding.

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/lez-programs/blob/90ca372de4ca829623712fa86c540924ed1b53cc/ata/core/src/lib.rs#L21-L35

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/lez-programs/blob/90ca372de4ca829623712fa86c540924ed1b53cc/ata/src/transfer.rs#L7-L54

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/logos-execution-zone/pull/414

### `f6168fe` test(amm): assert pool pda claim on new definition

This is guardrail coverage for the new PDA claim contract introduced by LEZ. AMM tests now assert not only the pool data, but also the exact `Claim::Pda(...)` metadata that makes the pool claim valid.

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/lez-programs/blob/90ca372de4ca829623712fa86c540924ed1b53cc/amm/src/tests.rs#L1927-L1936

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/logos-execution-zone/pull/414

### `7c34caa` test(ata): assert create chained call details

This is guardrail coverage for the ATA-to-token bridge contract. ATA create now proves the exact authorization and PDA seed it passes into token initialization, so a future refactor cannot silently break that handoff.

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/lez-programs/blob/90ca372de4ca829623712fa86c540924ed1b53cc/ata/src/tests.rs#L75-L96

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/logos-execution-zone/pull/414

### `c989253` test(token): cover claim migration expectations

This commit finishes the token-side migration coverage and makes the new claim rules visible in unit tests. It covers both sides of the conditional behavior: default destinations require a claim, while already initialized destinations do not.

https://github.com/logos-blockchain/lez-programs/blob/90ca372de4ca829623712fa86c540924ed1b53cc/token/src/tests.rs#L577-L730

head: 237b36560d91b57ec1b8948b4425cdba7ff25bb3
title: `Exam mode`: Fix intermittent live event delivery and test run submission errors
body:
### Summary

Fixes four critical exam mode bugs where (1) live events (announcements, working time changes, problem statement updates) were intermittently not delivered to students during exams, and (2) submitting text/modeling/file-upload exercises during instructor test runs failed with errors.

### Checklist
#### General
- [x] I tested **all** changes and their related features with **all** corresponding user types on a test server.
- [x] Language: I followed the [guidelines for inclusive, diversity-sensitive, and appreciative language](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/language).
- [x] I chose a title conforming to the [naming conventions for pull requests](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/development-process#pr-naming-conventions).

#### Server
- [x] **Important**: I implemented the changes with a [very good performance](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/performance) and prevented too many (unnecessary) and too complex database calls.
- [x] I **strictly** followed the principle of **data economy** for all database calls.
- [x] I **strictly** followed the [server coding and design guidelines](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/server-development) and the [REST API guidelines](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/rest-api).
- [x] I added multiple integration tests (Spring) related to the features (with a high test coverage).
- [x] I documented the Java code using JavaDoc style.

#### Client
- [x] **Important**: I implemented the changes with a very good performance, prevented too many (unnecessary) REST calls and made sure the UI is responsive, even with large data (e.g. using paging).
- [x] I **strictly** followed the principle of **data economy** for all client-server REST calls.
- [x] I **strictly** followed the [client coding guidelines](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/client-development).
- [x] I added multiple integration tests (Vitest) related to the features (with a high test coverage), while following the [test guidelines](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/client-tests).
- [x] I documented the TypeScript code using JSDoc style.

### Motivation and Context

During the Artemis 9.0.0 testing session, four critical bugs were found in exam mode:

- **#12423**: Exam announcements were intermittently not shown to students
- **#12424**: Submitting text/modeling/file-upload exercises during test runs resulted in errors
- **#12428**: Problem statement updates were intermittently not propagated to students
- **#12435**: Changing exam duration was intermittently not reflected in student clients

Closes #12423, closes #12424, closes #12428, closes #12435

### Description

**Bug 1 — Intermittent live event loss (#12423, #12428, #12435):**

Root causes identified in `ExamParticipationLiveEventsService`:
1. Both the WebSocket subscription and REST historical fetch were delayed by 5 seconds after the student exam loaded. Events arriving in that window were completely missed.
2. `fetchPreviousExamEvents()` overwrote the in-memory events array with the HTTP response, discarding any events that had arrived via WebSocket between the request and response.

Fix: Subscribe to WebSocket topics immediately (no delay). Only delay the REST historical fetch by 2 seconds to spread server load. Merge fetched events with existing ones instead of overwriting, using a Set-based deduplication to preserve WebSocket-delivered events.

**Bug 2 — Working time events sent before DB save (#12435):**

In `ExamService.updateStudentExamsAndRescheduleExercises()`, WebSocket notifications were sent inside the loop before `saveAll()`. If a student's client immediately called the REST fallback after receiving the WebSocket message, the event might not be in the database yet.

Fix: Save all student exams to the database first, then send WebSocket notifications.

**Bug 3 — Test run submission errors (#12424):**

`ParticipationService.findOneByExerciseAndStudentLoginWithEagerSubmissionsAnyState()` only looked for `testRun=false` participations for regular exam exercises. An instructor performing a test run has `testRun=true` on their participation, so the method returned empty → HTTP 424 error.

Fix: When no graded participation is found for a regular exam exercise, fall back to checking for `testRun=true` participations.

**Additional hardening from code review:**
- Cancel pending `setTimeout` for REST fetch when student exam changes (prevents stale fetch)
- Reset identity fields (studentExamId, examId, etc.) when navigating away from exam
- Sort merged events by date for consistent display order

### Steps for Testing

#### Test Run Submission (#12424)
Prerequisites:
- 1 Instructor

1. Create an exam with text, modeling, and file-upload exercises
2. Start a test run as the instructor
3. Navigate to each exercise and make changes
4. Verify that saving each exercise works without errors
5. Submit the entire test run — verify it succeeds

#### Live Event Delivery (#12423, #12428, #12435)
Prerequisites:
- 1 Instructor
- 1 Student
- Simultaneously logged in with both users in different browsers

1. Create an exam with at least one exercise and register the student
2. Start the exam and participate as the student
3. As instructor, make an announcement → verify the student sees it immediately
4. As instructor, change the problem statement → verify the student sees the update
5. As instructor, change the exam duration → verify the student's timer updates
6. Repeat steps 3-5 multiple times to check for intermittent failures

### Review Progress
#### Code Review
- [x] Code Review 1
- [x] Code Review 2
#### Exam Mode Test
- [ ] Test 1
- [ ] Test 2

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Immediate WebSocket subscription with delayed REST backfill, event replay and deduplication for exam participation.
  * Fallback handling to surface appropriate participation data for regular exam exercises.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Persist working-time updates before emitting live notifications to ensure correct client updates.
  * Only fetch missed events on real reconnections to avoid unnecessary backfills.

* **Tests**
  * Added tests for test-run submissions, reconnection behavior, and event-merge regressions.

* **Chores**
  * Improved local e2e teardown to ensure ports are cleanly released.

head: f828e2d8d4c5ace8c7aa70389e52c7e61761c14d
title: Aktivitetspenger inntektsrapportering
body:
This pull request introduces support for "inntektsrapportering" (income reporting) for the "Aktivitetspenger" benefit throughout the codebase. It adds new Kafka topics, extends enums and services, and implements new API endpoints and data models to handle income reporting submissions, including integration with the task management system.

The most important changes are:

**Kafka Topics and Configuration**
* Added three new Kafka topics for handling different stages of "aktivitetspenger-inntektsrapportering" (`mottatt`, `preprosessert`, `cleanup`) in `aktivitetspenger-inntektsrapportering-topics.yml`, with appropriate ACLs and retention policies.
* Registered the new topic in `Topics.kt` and updated the topic selection logic to handle the new `AKTIVITETSPENGER_INNTEKTSRAPPORTERING` type. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-81c50ef5bed7712d8e2e6dbe22dd4503af3ab806c70c1d0181b21efab9cad3b2R38) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-81c50ef5bed7712d8e2e6dbe22dd4503af3ab806c70c1d0181b21efab9cad3b2R62)

**Domain Model and API**
* Introduced `AktivitetspengerInntektsrapportering` and `AktivitetspengerInntektsrapporteringInnsending` data classes to represent and process income reporting submissions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4e656c3718b45418384544295f09723b186c40f7b987e71b0ff43c8e733b4db2R1-R17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c64c0a0381387e10349d506f520be966d0071b378b7835f62a17fd725d7680eaR1-R76)
* Added a new POST endpoint `/inntektsrapportering/innsending` in `AktivitetspengerController` to receive income reporting submissions.

**Service Layer and Integration**
* Implemented the `inntektrapportering` method in `AktivitetspengerService` to handle submissions: validates, registers, sends metrics, and marks related tasks as completed using `UngBrukerdialogApiService`.
* Integrated with the task management system to fetch task periods and mark tasks as solved after income reporting is received. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-21a79806cca2803fba2a7999a021f690656e4623a2be288e1e651d4a18f714c9R35) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-21a79806cca2803fba2a7999a021f690656e4623a2be288e1e651d4a18f714c9R76-R121)

**Enums and Supporting Structures**
* Extended `Ytelse`, `YtelseType`, and `KafkaStreamName` enums to support the new income reporting flow for Aktivitetspenger, including mapping topics to the new type. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-dbe2ba52d0c42fe8e7f07082cd545c62e2b498177e0b7268ee16f2b13378415cR67) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-dbe2ba52d0c42fe8e7f07082cd545c62e2b498177e0b7268ee16f2b13378415cR92) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-eac334b6458b0e89981131a5806709b194ae23b3f970d3dce8ab2315787a9513L187-R194) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-5fbf2360f35cacd01444cd957c7ed98d25c44513834cc9555c1d5664d3e281ccR121-R125) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-1b714cf039c2fdec162bc757b2b540d606a799a8e4448e4eb33491d05eafa710R29)
* Updated PDF generator logic to handle the new reporting type.

These changes establish the full technical foundation for receiving, processing, and tracking "inntektsrapportering" for Aktivitetspenger in the system.

head: 343e5688641d1d989d8535e0276a08a1adc9ede8
title: Add support for MCP Catalogs from private repos and non-github repos
body:
## Summary

Addresses #6341 #5543

Adds support for pulling MCP catalogs from private git repositories, and generalizes catalog source URL support beyond GitHub to any HTTPS git host.

### Credential storage
- Admins can supply a Personal Access Token (PAT) when adding a git source URL via the UI
- Tokens are stored securely in the GPTScript credential store (keyed by catalog UID + URL hash), never in the resource spec
- The API returns `"*"` as a presence indicator — the actual token is never exposed

### Git platform support
- **GitHub**: supported with or without `.git` suffix; falls back to `GITHUB_AUTH_TOKEN` env var for default catalog if no per-URL token is configured
- **GitLab**: supported with or without `.git` suffix; supports subgroups (`group/subgroup/repo.git`)
- **Self-hosted**: supported with `.git` suffix (e.g. `https://git.example.com/org/repo.git`)

### Repository size limits
- **GitHub**: pre-clone size check via GitHub API (fast, no bandwidth wasted)
- **GitLab**: pre-clone size check via GitLab projects API when a token is available (`read_api` scope required, but 403 error is ignored)
- **All other hosts**: clone is monitored in real time with a custom FS

### Other changes
- Context is propagated from the controller sync request through all HTTP calls and the git clone
- URL with `.git` suffix is handled correctly (stripped before constructing clone URL and API calls)
- Tooltip in the UI explains supported URL formats
- Enable editing in the UI. Most code for it existed already

## Testing guide
- [x] Add a public GitHub repo as a source URL — verify sync works
- [x] Add a private GitHub repo with a PAT — verify sync works and token is not visible in the UI after saving
- [x] Add a private GitLab repo (`https://gitlab.com/org/repo.git`) with a PAT — verify sync works
- [x] Add a GitLab repo with subgroups (`https://gitlab.com/group/subgroup/repo.git`) — verify sync works
- [x] Add a URL with `.git` suffix — verify it works the same as without
- [x] Remove a source URL that has a stored token — verify the credential is cleaned up
- [x] Verify `GITHUB_AUTH_TOKEN` env var still works as a fallback for GitHub default catalog when no per-URL token is set
- [x] Attempt to clone large repository that isn't on Github or Gitlab (`https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git`)

head: e4127110f2d9dcf4d8ca9bb24d6f92ce10ac1013
title: fix: adapt audit client to npmjs /advisories/bulk endpoint
body:
The legacy `/-/npm/v1/security/audits{,/quick}` endpoints have been retired by npmjs.org. This PR rewires the audit client to the replacement `/-/npm/v1/security/advisories/bulk` endpoint.

The new endpoint is not a drop-in rename — the request and response contracts are both different:

- **Request**: a flat `{ pkgName: [versions] }` map. `lockfileToAuditRequest` walks the lockfile once and builds the POST body directly; there is no more nested `AuditTree`.
- **Response**: only `id`, `url`, `title`, `severity`, `vulnerable_versions`, and `cwe` per advisory. Everything else the old endpoint returned is computed locally:
  - `findings[].paths` are walked from the lockfile (skipped entirely when the response is empty; the second walk intentionally avoids `@pnpm/lockfile.walker`'s global dedup so alternate install chains to the same shared dep aren't dropped).
  - `metadata.vulnerabilities` counts advisories per severity.
  - `metadata.dependencies` / `devDependencies` / `optionalDependencies` / `totalDependencies` come from a classified lockfile walk; the classifier respects `--prod`/`--dev` include flags when deciding whether a subgraph is reachable non-optionally.
  - `patched_versions` is inferred from the vulnerable range for common `<X.Y.Z` / `<=X.Y.Z` shapes so `audit --fix` can still produce usable overrides; left `undefined` when inference fails.
  - `github_advisory_id` is parsed from the advisory URL and canonicalized to the github.com form (uppercase `GHSA-` prefix, lowercase suffix).
  - `info` severity is now supported end-to-end (severity type, `--audit-level`, filters, colors).

## Breaking changes (v11)

- Private registries that do not implement `/advisories/bulk` now fail with `AuditEndpointNotExistsError`.
- CVE-based filtering is replaced with GHSA-based filtering, since the bulk endpoint does not return CVE identifiers:
  - `auditConfig.ignoreCves` → `auditConfig.ignoreGhsas` (the old key is no longer recognized).
  - `pnpm audit --ignore <id>` and `--ignore-unfixable` now read and write GHSAs.
  - Migration: replace each `CVE-YYYY-NNNNN` in `auditConfig.ignoreCves` with the matching `GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx` (visible in the `More info` column of `pnpm audit` output) under `auditConfig.ignoreGhsas`.
- `--ignore-unfixable` now only targets advisories whose patched range couldn't be inferred — the only "no fix available" signal the bulk endpoint provides.
- `AuditReport` and `AuditAdvisory` are trimmed to just the fields the audit client actually populates:
  - `AuditReport`: `advisories` + `metadata` only (`actions` and `muted` removed).
  - `AuditAdvisory`: `findings`, `id`, `title`, `module_name`, `vulnerable_versions`, `patched_versions?`, `severity`, `cwe`, `github_advisory_id`, `url`. Dropped: `cves`, `created`, `updated`, `deleted`, `access`, `overview`, `recommendation`, `references`, `found_by`, `reported_by`, `metadata`.
  - `AuditAction`, `AuditResolution`, `AuditActionRecommendation` removed (no consumers).

## Hardening

- Response body validated: non-object / malformed JSON / non-array package buckets all surface as `ERR_PNPM_AUDIT_BAD_RESPONSE` with a body excerpt. Advisory `id` must be a finite number and `severity` must be a known value before being indexed.
- Name-keyed records use `Object.create(null)` so a hostile/unusual package name can't trigger prototype pollution.
- GHSA ids canonicalized on both read and write so casing drift between config and registry doesn't mask ignores.
- `findings[].paths` are deduped and capped per (name, version) to keep pathologically shared graphs from blowing up memory.

## Internals

- `AuditTree` / `AuditNode` / `lockfileToAuditTree` removed. `lockfileToAuditIndex.ts` exports `lockfileToAuditRequest` (flat POST body + counts) and `buildAuditPathIndex` (only invoked when the response has advisories).
- `AuditAdvisory.findings` is now `AuditFinding[]` (was an unintended 1-tuple).
- Top-level test fixtures regenerated from real `registry.npmjs.org` responses; synthetic `update-*` fixtures converted in place to bulk shape.

head: a867cca3f7a1f9844445f89d1c0b005048fba9af
title: Add `MethodForwardingHandler` for Relation method forwarding
body:
## Issue to Solve

When calling Builder methods on Eloquent Relations (e.g., `$relation->where(...)`), Psalm resolves the method via `@mixin Builder` and returns `Builder<Phone>` instead of `HasOne<Phone, User>`. QueryBuilder-only methods like `orderBy` fall to `__call` with no param validation and `mixed` return type.

Closes #637, closes #190

## Solution Description

New `MethodForwardingHandler` in `src/Handlers/Magic/` replaces `RelationsMethodHandler` with two resolution paths:

- **Path 1 (Mixin interception):** Intercepts `@mixin`-resolved calls on Builder/QueryBuilder, detects the original Relation caller via node type provider, and returns the Relation's generic type for fluent methods.
- **Path 2 (`__call` forwarding):** Handles QueryBuilder-only methods (orderBy, limit, groupBy, etc.) that fall through to `__call`. Provides both return types and method params via `MethodParamsProviderInterface`.

Three files:
- `ForwardingRule` — immutable value object describing the forwarding hop
- `ReturnTypeResolver` — self-return detection with per-method cache
- `MethodForwardingHandler` — dual-interface handler (return type + params)

Covers all 14 Relation subclasses. No use of `ProxyMethodReturnTypeProvider::executeFakeCall()` (avoids 50GB+ memory explosion on large codebases). No manual method list to maintain — dynamically checks `declaring_method_ids` on Builder/QueryBuilder.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests cover the change (type test in `tests/Type/` and/or unit test in `tests/Unit/`)
- [x] Documentation is updated (if needed, otherwise remove this item)

head: b5bbf831815009e4906eb69960364dc26102306c
title: Detect missing views through View facade calls
body:
## Issue to Solve

Plugin handlers registered for a service class (e.g., `Illuminate\View\Factory`) don't fire when the same method is called through a facade (`View::make()`). Psalm's `MethodReturnTypeProvider` uses exact class-name matching, so `View::make()` bypasses any handler registered only for `Factory`.

## Related

Partially addresses #591 (facade static calls only; model `__callStatic`, `@method` proxies, and taint propagation through proxies are not yet covered)

## Solution Description

Add `FacadeMapProvider` — a registry that maps service classes to their facade/alias class names at plugin boot time. Handlers call `FacadeMapProvider::getFacadeClasses()` in `getClassLikeNames()` to register for both the service class and its facades.

Any handler can opt into facade support with one line:
```php
return [Factory::class, ...FacadeMapProvider::getFacadeClasses(Factory::class)];
```

Applied to `MissingViewHandler` as the first use case — `View::make('nonexistent')` now emits `MissingView`, same as `view('nonexistent')` already did.

Also includes: CI benchmark workflow fix, deprecated php-parser class replacements.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests cover the change (type test in `tests/Type/` and/or unit test in `tests/Unit/`)

title: Issue #18 - adding word-based statistics
body:
This PR addresses issue #18 by adding word-based statistics, very similar to what was done with phrases. A list of the top 25 most-frequently-occurring words is gathered when statistics are loaded. Short words (currently defined as having fewer than 5 characters) are excluded from the search, because they are not interesting. The top 25 results are displayed on a new "Most common words" tab in the `StatisticsDialog`. The user is also offered a simple search form, where on-the-fly searching for specific words is possible. The minimum word length is ignored when searching for specific words.

Additionally, a count of globally unique words (including short words) is calculated during statistics loading. This is also displayed on the Words tab. Code was added to allow this feature to be disabled easily later, but currently it is always enabled.

head: 8fc7cd32904240c2c841e70aef2ba5c3bb659ffd
title: Add resolution support for image formats (JPEG, TIFF, PNG, BMP) along with unit parsing
body:
Solution for https://github.com/sdsykes/fastimage/issues/164

### Summary

- Adds `FastImage.resolution(uri)` class method returning `[[x, y], :units]` or `nil`
- Adds `#resolution` and `#resolution_units` instance methods returning the components separately
- Supports JPEG (JFIF APP0), PNG (pHYs chunk), BMP (DIB header), and TIFF (EXIF IFD rational tags)
- Extends `GoodFixtures` with a resolution column and adds a `test_should_report_resolution_correctly` sweep test covering all fixture files

### Supported formats and units

| Format | Source | Possible units |
|--------|--------|----------------|
| JPEG | JFIF APP0 segment | `:inches`, `:centimeters`, `:no_units` |
| PNG | pHYs chunk | `:meters`, `:no_units` |
| BMP | DIB header (`XPelsPerMeter`/`YPelsPerMeter`) | `:meters` |
| TIFF | EXIF `XResolution`/`YResolution` rational tags | `:inches`, `:centimeters`, `:no_units` |

Formats without resolution metadata (GIF, WebP, SVG, HEIC, AVIF, JXL, PSD, ICO) return `nil` for both methods.

### API

```ruby
# Class method — returns [[x, y], :units] or nil
FastImage.resolution("image.jpg")  # => [[72, 72], :inches]
FastImage.resolution("image.png")  # => nil

# Instance methods
fi = FastImage.new("image.tiff")
fi.resolution        # => [72.0, 72.0]
fi.resolution_units  # => :inches
```

### Notes

- TIFF resolution values are `Float` (stored as RATIONAL numerator/denominator in EXIF); other formats return `Integer`
- BMP returns `nil` when both PPM values are zero (unspecified) or when the file uses the older `BITMAPCOREHEADER` which has no resolution fields
- The EXIF parser was extended with named tag/data-type constants and a two-pass approach to read RATIONAL offsets after the IFD scan

head: 41d750067fc7a39eb29f6a530cf0d4ae0f8bdb41
title: feat: pluggable auth providers — add AT Protocol, refactor GitHub/Google
body: ## What does this PR do? Introduces a **pluggable auth provider system** and uses it to add **AT Protocol authentication** as the first plugin-based provider. GitHub and Google OAuth are refactored from hardcoded buttons into the same provider interface. All auth methods — passkey, AT Protocol, GitHub, Google — are equal options on the login page and setup wizard. ### Auth provider descriptor Every provider implements `AuthProviderDescriptor`: ```ts emdash({ authProviders: [atproto(), github(), google()], }) ``` Each descriptor declares an `adminEntry` (React components for login/setup UI), optional `routes` (Astro route handlers), and `publicRoutes` (middleware bypass prefixes). Components are distributed to the admin app via a `virtual:emdash/auth-providers` Vite virtual module. ### What changed > **Scope note:** The entire pluggable auth provider system is new in this PR — none of it existed on `main`. The pre-existing `AuthDescriptor` / `AuthProviderModule` (transparent auth for Cloudflare Access) is unchanged. **New pluggable infrastructure (core):** - `AuthProviderDescriptor` / `AuthRouteDescriptor` types in `auth/types.ts` - `authProviders` config field on `EmDashConfig` - `virtual:emdash/auth-providers` virtual module with `generateAuthProvidersModule()` - `injectAuthProviderRoutes()` for generic route injection from descriptors - Dynamic public routes in auth middleware (merged from all providers) - `AuthProviderContext` in admin for distributing provider UI components - Public `/_emdash/api/auth/mode` endpoint returning available providers - `emdash/api/route-utils` public export for API utilities used by plugin routes - `finalizeSetup()` shared helper for setup completion (idempotent, used by all auth callbacks) **Shared OAuth user creation (`@emdash-cms/auth`):** - `findOrCreateOAuthUser()` extracted as a shared export — handles OAuth account lookup, email auto-linking, and user creation with `canSelfSignup` policy - Used by all OAuth providers (GitHub, Google, AT Protocol) for consistent signup gating and role assignment **Login page:** - Removed hardcoded `OAUTH_PROVIDERS` array - All providers render from virtual module via `useAuthProviderList()` - Providers with `LoginButton` show in a button grid; those with `LoginForm` expand inline on click **Setup wizard:** - All configured auth providers appear as equal options alongside passkey - Clicking a provider button either navigates directly (GitHub/Google OAuth) or expands a form (AT Protocol handle input) - OAuth callback is setup-aware: first user becomes admin, site config is persisted, setup is marked complete - First-user admin creation uses a database transaction to prevent TOCTOU race conditions - URL error params displayed in a banner (previously errors were silently lost) **AT Protocol (new — `@emdash-cms/plugin-atproto`):** - `atproto()` returns `AuthProviderDescriptor` with routes for login, callback, setup-admin, and client metadata - Route handlers live in the plugin package (`@emdash-cms/plugin-atproto/routes/*`), not in core — removing the plugin removes the routes - `LoginButton` (compact butterfly icon), `LoginForm` (handle input), `SetupStep` exported from `@emdash-cms/plugin-atproto/admin` - Uses `@atcute/oauth-node-client` with PKCE (public client, no key management needed) - First user becomes Admin during setup; subsequent users get the configured default role (Subscriber by default) - `allowedDIDs` allowlist for access control by permanent DID identifiers - `allowedHandles` allowlist with wildcard support for org-level domain gating (e.g., `*.mycompany.com`). Handle ownership is independently verified via DNS-over-HTTPS and HTTP well-known resolution using `@atcute/identity-resolver` — the PDS's handle claim is never trusted directly - If both are set, matching either list grants access - Uses shared `findOrCreateOAuthUser()` with `canSelfSignup` policy for consistent signup gating **GitHub / Google (refactored to descriptors):** - `github()` and `google()` return `AuthProviderDescriptor` with `adminEntry` pointing to `-admin.tsx` components - `LoginButton` components with provider icons, reusing core's existing `[provider]` OAuth routes - No new routes needed — they reuse core's shared OAuth infrastructure **OAuth error handling:** - OAuth initiation route checks `Referer` to redirect errors back to the originating page (setup wizard vs login) - Error messages include which env vars need to be set when a provider isn't configured ### Configuration ```ts import { atproto } from "@emdash-cms/plugin-atproto/auth"; import { github } from "emdash/auth/providers/github"; import { google } from "emdash/auth/providers/google"; emdash({ authProviders: [atproto(), github(), google()], }) ``` AT Protocol options: ```ts atproto({ // Permanent DID-based allowlist allowedDIDs: ["did:plc:abc123"], // Domain-based allowlist (independently verified via DNS/HTTP) allowedHandles: ["*.mycompany.com", "alice.bsky.social"], // Default role for new users (default: 10 / Subscriber) defaultRole: 20, // Contributor }) ``` ### New routes (AT Protocol) - `POST /_emdash/api/auth/atproto/login` — initiate OAuth flow (handle → PDS authorization URL) - `GET /_emdash/api/auth/atproto/callback` — handle PDS redirect, create/find user, establish session - `POST /_emdash/api/setup/atproto-admin` — setup wizard flow - `GET /.well-known/atproto-client-metadata.json` — client metadata (PDS fetches this) ## Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] Feature (requires [approved Discussion](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/discussions/categories/ideas)) - [ ] Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] Documentation - [ ] Performance improvement - [ ] Tests - [ ] Chore (dependencies, CI, tooling) ## Checklist - [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes - [x] `pnpm --silent lint:json | jq '.diagnostics | length'` returns 0 - [x] `pnpm test` passes (or targeted tests for my change) - [x] `pnpm format` has been run - [x] I have added/updated tests for my changes (if applicable) - [x] I have added a [changeset](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#changesets) (if this PR changes a published package) - [x] New features link to an approved Discussion: https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/discussions/320 ## AI-generated code disclosure - [x] This PR includes AI-generated code ## Screenshots / test output ### Test results (2026-04-08) **emdash (core):** 2096 tests, 113 files — all passing ``` Test Files 113 passed (113) Tests 2096 passed (2096) ``` **@emdash-cms/plugin-atproto:** 76 tests, 7 files — all passing ``` ✓ tests/plugin.test.ts (5 tests) 3ms ✓ tests/atproto.test.ts (3 tests) 4ms ✓ tests/auth.test.ts (15 tests) 9ms ✓ tests/standard-site.test.ts (21 tests) 5ms ✓ tests/bluesky.test.ts (18 tests) 15ms ✓ tests/resolve-handle.test.ts (3 tests) 15ms ✓ tests/oauth-client.test.ts (11 tests) 123ms Test Files 7 passed (7) Tests 76 passed (76) ``` **@emdash-cms/auth:** 41 tests, 2 files — all passing ``` Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 41 passed (41) ``` **@emdash-cms/admin:** ⚠️ Browser tests failing due to Playwright infrastructure issue (pre-existing `@vitest/browser-playwright` setup error, not a regression from this PR).

head: 4177c9e48dd263a9f2f82299348a77b1aef4abd1
title: Make matching output fully deterministic across runs
body:
## Summary

- Pre-sort packets by track number before matching, so each batch contains consecutive same-track packets
- Replace channel-based worker pool with deterministic batched workers (fixed 64-packet batches, atomic counter work queue)
- Each batch is processed sequentially by a single goroutine with batch-local locality state — no shared `trackHints` or `regionsMu` in the hot path
- Deterministic inter-batch edge sync retries boundary NALs that had hash misses using locality from adjacent batches
- Batch results merged in batch-index order for deterministic output

## Why this is deterministic

1. Fixed batch boundaries → same packets in same batches every run
2. Sequential intra-batch processing → deterministic locality chain
3. No cross-batch coverage reads → no scheduling-dependent NAL skipping
4. Ordered result merge → `mergeRegions()` always gets the same input

## Test plan

- [x] All existing tests pass (`go test ./...`)
- [ ] Run `mkvdup create` twice on same Blu-ray inputs and verify `.mkvdup` files are byte-identical
- [ ] Compare match statistics to ensure no regression in coverage
- [ ] Test with `GOMAXPROCS=1` and `GOMAXPROCS=8` to verify same output

Closes #179

head: b227aff048155b8d2a8426b4d84bcec4504e7c01
title: Persistent named palettes with tabbed drawer, export, and UX polish
body:
Replaces the flat auto-history drawer with a tabbed palette system: a persistent auto-history palette at index 0, plus user-created named palettes. Several behavioral bugs were caught and fixed across iterative review.

## Data layer
- New `Palette` model (`id`, `name?`, `pairs`, `createdAt`); auto-history is `palettes[0]` where `name == nil`
- `migrateHistoryToPalettes()` merges legacy `colorHistory` into `palettes[0].pairs` rather than overwriting
- `Defaults[.activePaletteIndex]` tracks the active tab; clamped to 0 on out-of-range

## Palette management (`Eyedroppers`)
- `savePalette`, `renamePalette`, `deletePalette`, `addCurrentToPalette`, `deleteChipFromPalette`
- `swap()` only calls `pushUndo()` when on auto-history (index 0) — named-palette swaps no longer corrupt the undo stack
- `savePalette` sets `activeHistoryID = current.id` so the new chip is selected immediately
- `deleteChipFromPalette` nils `activeHistoryID` when the removed pair was active
- `deletePalette` calls `restoreAutoHistorySelection()` after clamping to index 0, and decrements `activePaletteIndex` when deleting a palette before the active one

## Drawer UI
- `PaletteTabBar` with inline create/rename via `PaletteNameField`; auto-history tab shows a clock icon
- Tab switch uses directional vertical slide — `slideDirection` is set via `@Binding` in the button action *before* `activePaletteIndex` changes, avoiding the one-frame-behind issue that `onChange` caused
- `isAutoHistory` derived from `activePalette?.isAutoHistory ?? false`; `activePaletteIndex` is clamped back to 0 async when out of range
- Context-menu remove label switches between `textHistoryRemove` and `textPaletteRemoveChip` based on `isAutoHistory`

## Export
- `Exporter.paletteToJSON` serialises pairs; auto-history entries include an ISO 8601 `date` field
- `ISO8601DateFormatter` hoisted out of the `pairs.map` closure (one allocation per export, not per pair)
- Filename strips `/`, `:`, `\` before `NSSavePanel`; write errors surface via `NSAlert`

## UI polish
- Toolbar tooltips include keyboard shortcuts: preview (P), compliance (C), history (H)
- Compliance button: `checkmark.shield.fill` when active vs `checkmark.shield` when inactive

head: c60823535d6086eb09f11a009f289e908ebf4758
title: fix(qa-remediation): stop false remediation loops from docs-only rounds and carried known issues
body:
Fixes #357

## What

Stops false remediation loops caused by two interacting bugs: (1) documentation-only remediation rounds failing the change-evidence gate because only committed diffs were checked, and (2) carried known issues with no explicit outcome model forcing blind extra rounds.

16 files modified (+2105 -170 lines), with the majority being new BATS regression tests (1202+ new lines in `tests/qa-result-gate.bats` alone).

## Why

The root cause was a two-part invariant failure in the QA remediation pipeline:

1. **Evidence validation was commit-only**: `qa-result-gate.sh` validated round-local change evidence using only `git diff` against committed hashes. Documentation-only rounds (process-exception acceptances, remediation plans/summaries) had `commit_hashes: []` and recorded their artifacts in `files_modified` — but the gate couldn't verify artifacts that existed only as worktree changes, not commits. This caused `qa_gate_round_change_evidence_unavailable` on every docs-only round, forcing infinite reruns.

2. **Known issues had no disposition model**: The carried known-issues flow had no way to record whether an issue was `resolved`, `accepted-process-exception`, or `unresolved`. Without explicit outcomes, the gate treated every carried issue as potentially unresolved, which — combined with the evidence bug — created a loop: round produces docs-only output → gate rejects evidence → new round → same docs-only output → infinite cycle.

The architectural fix addresses both invariants: evidence validation now uses a union of committed diff plus current worktree paths (scoped to remediation artifacts and original-plan amendments), and the known-issues lifecycle now has an explicit disposition model that flows through materialization, gate evaluation, and STATE.md persistence.

## How

### Core engine changes

- **`scripts/qa-result-gate.sh`**: Added worktree evidence fallback scoped to recorded remediation artifacts and valid original-plan amendment targets. Added known-issues guards in both metadata-only and non-metadata-only PROCEED_TO_UAT branches that check live registry coverage against round outcomes. Updated `json_object_array_dispositions_match()` to use `(test, file, error, disposition)` identity tuple.

- **`scripts/qa-remediation-state.sh`**: Added `input_mode` field (`findings`, `known-issues`, `both`) to distinguish round input types. Broadened issue identity key from `(test, file)` to `(test, file, error)` for correct deduplication. Added `known_issues_input` and `known_issue_outcomes` passthrough in round initialization.

- **`scripts/track-known-issues.sh`**: `merge_issue_sets()` and `replace_issue_set()` now propagate `.disposition` from incoming issues to existing registry entries. `promote_todos()` rewrites already-tracked STATE.md lines when disposition changes to `accepted-process-exception`, using awk for literal string replacement.

- **`scripts/phase-detect.sh`**: Added `promote-todos` call after `sync-verification` state to ensure known-issue dispositions reach STATE.md.

### Template and prompt changes

- **`templates/REMEDIATION-PLAN.md`**: Added canonical `known_issues_input` and `known_issues_resolutions` structured sections.

- **`templates/REMEDIATION-SUMMARY.md`**: Added `known_issue_outcomes` section with explicit status model: `resolved`, `accepted-process-exception`, `unresolved`.

- **`commands/vibe.md`** and **`references/execute-protocol.md`**: Updated warning text to describe "recorded change evidence that could not be verified" (not omitted `files_modified`), and documented that documentation-only/process-exception rounds may be proven by round-local remediation artifact changes.

- **`commands/verify.md`**: `--skip-qa` path now runs `qa-result-gate.sh` and checks gate routing before proceeding to UAT. Split malformed/unresolved known-issues messages.

### Test and contract changes

- **`testing/verify-commands-contract.sh`**: Updated contract to check for both separate `unreadable` and `unresolved` known-issues guard messages.
- **`testing/verify-plan-filename-convention.sh`**: Updated convention for new template sections.
- **`tests/discovered-issues-surfacing.bats`**: Split grep for separated messages.

## Acceptance Criteria Verification

1. **Git-backed docs-only regression test**: Satisfied by `tests/qa-result-gate.bats` test "docs-only round with remediation summary as only change is accepted via worktree fallback" — creates a Git repo with `commit_hashes: []`, `files_modified` pointing to a remediation summary, and asserts `qa_gate_round_change_evidence_corroborated=true`.

2. **Union evidence validation with scoped worktree fallback**: Satisfied by `scripts/qa-result-gate.sh` lines implementing `_worktree_fallback_for_remediation_artifacts()` — only allows worktree fallback for paths matching remediation artifact or original-plan amendment patterns.

3. **Fail-closed protections intact**: Satisfied by existing and new BATS tests covering unresolved commit hashes, missing `round_started_at_commit`, stale anchors, malformed registries, and arbitrary docs/README changes.

4. **Updated warning text**: Satisfied by changes in `commands/vibe.md` and `references/execute-protocol.md` — both now describe "recorded change evidence that could not be verified."

5. **REMEDIATION-PLAN.md known-issue sections**: Satisfied by `templates/REMEDIATION-PLAN.md` `known_issues_input` and `known_issues_resolutions` sections anchored to existing issue shape.

6. **REMEDIATION-SUMMARY.md outcomes section**: Satisfied by `templates/REMEDIATION-SUMMARY.md` `known_issue_outcomes` with `resolved`/`accepted-process-exception`/`unresolved` status model.

7. **Three-way known-issue distinction**: Satisfied by `qa-remediation-state.sh` (materialization + input_mode), `track-known-issues.sh` (registry merge with disposition), and `qa-result-gate.sh` (live registry coverage guards). Tests cover all three categories.

8. **End-to-end input_mode coverage**: Satisfied by `tests/qa-remediation-state.bats` and `tests/qa-result-gate.bats` covering `input_mode=known-issues` and `input_mode=both`, including rounds that resolve/accept carried issues.

9. **Unresolved blocking known issues**: Satisfied by `tests/qa-result-gate.bats` test "known-issues gate blocks when live registry has new issue not covered by round outcomes" — asserts `qa_gate_routing=REMEDIATION_REQUIRED`.

10. **STATE.md persistence surface**: Satisfied by `track-known-issues.sh` `promote_todos()` — uses `[KNOWN-ISSUE]` tags in `STATE.md ## Todos`, with disposition rewrite for accepted issues. Tested in `tests/track-known-issues.bats` "promote-todos updates already-tracked issue with accepted disposition."

11. **All tests pass**: 2520 BATS tests pass, 0 failures, 32/32 contract checks, 1/1 lint check.

## Testing

- [x] Loaded plugin locally with `claude --plugin-dir .`
- [x] `bash testing/run-all.sh` passes: 2520 BATS, 32 contracts, 1 lint, 0 failures
- [x] New BATS tests cover docs-only evidence, known-issues input modes, disposition propagation, live registry coverage guards, and disposition match identity
- [x] Existing fail-closed tests unmodified and passing
- [x] ShellCheck clean on all modified scripts

## QA Summary

| Phase | Model | Rounds | Findings Fixed | False Positives |
|-------|-------|--------|----------------|-----------------|
| Primary QA | Claude Sonnet (qa-investigator) | 11 | ~10 | 0 |
| Cross-Model QA | GPT-5.4 (qa-investigator-gpt-54) | 7 | ~8 | 2 |

**False positives**:
1. Pre-existing markdown-lint warnings for unlabeled fenced code blocks in `commands/verify.md` — these are template expansion blocks in VBW command markdown, not introduced by this branch.
2. Newly observed issues being addressable in the current round — this is intentional behavior to avoid creating more remediation loops. The carried snapshot ensures all pre-existing issues are addressed; allowing the round to also address new issues is strictly better for termination.

body:
## Summary

Adds the `keycloak-migrate import-users` subcommand to the migration toolkit, closing #490.

## What this does

- Reads `users.json` produced by `keycloak-migrate transform`
- Two credential resolution modes:
  - **Cluster mode** (default): reads admin username/password from the Kubernetes secret generated by the operator (`{name}-admin-credentials`), verifies the Keycloak instance is `Ready` before importing
  - **Explicit flags** (`--username`/`--password`): for environments where RBAC doesn't permit secret reads
- Uses Keycloak's Partial Import API (`POST /admin/realms/{realm}/partialImport`) with chunked batching (default 500 users/batch) to stay within HTTP body limits
- **SKIP mode by default** — idempotent, re-running is safe even if users already exist
- Token lifecycle management with automatic refresh 30 s before expiry
- Hard fail on `errors > 0` in any batch response (non-atomic batches won't be rolled back automatically)
- File age check (default 24 h) to prevent importing stale exports

head: bc2ac1a4be2e0583597f65d48321802736e3d1a6
title: test: extract ComponentTestBase and remove real-time residue
body:
## Summary

Extract shared test helpers into `ComponentTestBase` and eliminate real-time residue (`CountDownLatch`, `Dispatchers.Default` polling) from all 5 component test classes. Closes #23, relates to wspulse/.github#22.

## Changes

- Add `ComponentTestBase` abstract class with `testScheduler`, `testClient`, `tearDown()`, `clientConfig()`, `waitUntil()` (scheduler-driven, no real delays), and `waitForPing()`.
- Migrate `BasicTest`, `CallbackTest`, `LifecycleTest`, `MiscTest`, `ReconnectTest` to extend `ComponentTestBase(TestCoroutineScheduler())`.
- Replace all `CountDownLatch` usage with `CompletableDeferred<Unit>`.
- Replace all FQN `kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest` with `runTest(StandardTestDispatcher(testScheduler))` to share the scheduler between base class and test scope.
- Remove duplicated `testClient` fields, `@AfterEach tearDown()` methods, and private helper functions from all 5 test classes.
- Remove unused imports from migrated files.
- Net diff: +154 / -339 lines (185 lines removed).

## Residual time-related patterns (all safe, non-flaky)

After the migration, a small number of time-related patterns remain. Each is bounded and will not cause flakiness:

| Pattern | Location | Why safe |
|---|---|---|
| `runBlocking` | `ComponentTestBase.tearDown()` | `@AfterEach` cannot be `suspend`; this is the required JUnit5 boundary. The client is already closed by the time teardown runs, so `done.await()` completes immediately. |
| `CompletableDeferred.await()` | All test bodies | Suspends, does not block a thread. The client uses `UnconfinedTestDispatcher`, which dispatches callbacks synchronously in the same call stack as `injectClose()` / `injectError()`. The deferred is always completed before `await()` is reached. |
| `withTimeout(1.seconds)` | `ReconnectTest` — close during reconnect | Runs inside `runTest`, so `1.seconds` is virtual time, not wall time. `transportDropSignal` is completed synchronously by `UnconfinedTestDispatcher` before the timeout fires. |
| `delay(60.seconds)` | `ReconnectTest` — slow dialer stub | Runs inside a coroutine on `UnconfinedTestDispatcher`. `client.close()` cancels it before the delay elapses; the test advances only 5 ms of virtual time. The 60-second delay is never actually waited on. |

## Checklist

### Required

- [x] `make check` passes (lint -> test)
- [x] Each commit represents exactly one logical change
- [x] Commit messages follow the format in `commit-message-instructions.md`
- [x] No unrelated code reformatting in this PR
