head: d60ff38a39b535f3ff24cfdc8ac843346de89d43
title: `Development`: Remove Hibernate L2 entity caches and disable second-level cache
body:
### Summary

Disables Hibernate second-level cache cluster-wide, strips the remaining 116 `@Cache(NONSTRICT_READ_WRITE)` annotations from 94 entity classes, removes the JCache bridge dependencies and code paths, adds an ArchUnit guardrail, and ships a long-form developer guideline documenting the policy and the canonical Spring `@Cacheable` + Hibernate event listener replacement pattern.

### Checklist

#### General
- [x] This is a small issue that I tested locally and was confirmed by another developer on a test server.
- [x] Language: I followed the [guidelines for inclusive, diversity-sensitive, and appreciative language](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/language).
- [x] I chose a title conforming to the [naming conventions for pull requests](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/development-process#pr-naming-conventions).

#### Server
- [x] **Important**: I implemented the changes with a [very good performance](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/performance) and prevented too many (unnecessary) and too complex database calls.
- [x] I **strictly** followed the principle of **data economy** for all database calls.
- [x] I **strictly** followed the [server coding and design guidelines](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/server-development) and the [REST API guidelines](https://docs.artemis.tum.de/developer/guidelines/rest-api).
- [x] I added multiple integration tests (Spring) related to the features (with a high test coverage).
- [x] I documented the Java code using JavaDoc style.

### Motivation and Context

Artemis runs in a 3-node Hazelcast cluster behind nginx with round-robin load balancing and no sticky sessions. Two production bugs (`#12574` cross-node stale `selectedOptions` in MC quiz submissions, `#12584` cross-node `ObjectNotFoundException` from stale entity-cache hits) and two prior cleanup PRs (`#12579` plus the extended sweep `0de9bdac67` / `a2fd873a38`) demonstrated that Hibernate `@Cache(NONSTRICT_READ_WRITE)` is unsafe on actively-mutated state in a clustered deployment.

Two attempts to address the bug class by switching to the stricter `READ_WRITE` strategy (`Result.feedbacks` in `99ac90a8ca`, `Lecture` entity in `3ecde55e5c`) were both reverted (`f571cfaa04`, `0aeccb54d7`). The rollback rationale captured in `f571cfaa04`:

> "There is no measured production regression from running without the cache on this collection, and the expected per-access gain (DB roundtrip vs Hazelcast cache roundtrip) is on the order of 1–2 ms with no hit-rate data to justify it."

That left ~70 reference entity classes still annotated with `NONSTRICT_READ_WRITE` (Course, Exercise, Lecture, Exam, User, Authority, plagiarism, modeling, text, atlas, science, communication, iris, lti, programming reference data, etc.) — a deferred Tier 3 audit that this PR closes.

Four structural facts about Artemis make Hibernate L2 unsafe and unhelpful in practice, regardless of the chosen concurrency strategy:

1. **No service-level `@Transactional`**. The project deliberately scopes transactions to repositories. There is no clean boundary inside a REST call to coordinate cache invalidation across multiple repository invocations.
2. **`spring.jpa.open-in-view: false`**. Per-repository-call sessions mean L2 only saves the *first* DB roundtrip per id per session.
3. **Heavy use of `@Modifying @Query`**. Bulk DML statements bypass Hibernate cache invalidation entirely; both `NONSTRICT_READ_WRITE` and `READ_WRITE` leak stale entries.
4. **Multi-node Hazelcast cluster, no sticky sessions**. Cross-node invalidation propagates asynchronously; under load the staleness window is observable as user-visible bugs.

### Description

**Code changes (94 entity files, 116 annotations removed, 188 unused imports removed):**
- All remaining `@Cache(usage = CacheConcurrencyStrategy.NONSTRICT_READ_WRITE)` annotations stripped from entity classes and associations across `assessment/`, `core/`, `atlas/`, `programming/`, `exercise/`, `exam/`, `lecture/`, `communication/`, `tutorialgroup/`, `plagiarism/`, `iris/`, `text/`, `lti/`, `modeling/`, and `quiz/` domain packages.

**Configuration:**
- `application.yml`: `hibernate.cache.use_second_level_cache: false`; removed the JCache region factory / provider / `missing_cache_strategy` properties; kept `hibernate.cache.hazelcast.instance_name` (still consumed by `HazelcastConfiguration` via `@Value`).
- `application-buildagent.yml`: untouched (defense in depth).
- `src/test/resources/config/application.yml`: refreshed obsolete comment.
- `build.gradle`: dropped `hibernate-jcache:7.2.12.Final` and `javax.cache:cache-api:1.1.1`.

**Hazelcast / metrics cleanup:**
- `HazelcastConfiguration`: removed `enableJCacheStatistics()` and its call, the `javax.cache.Cache` branch in `bindMetricsToMicrometer`, the `de.tum.cit.aet.artemis.*.domain.*` wildcard `MapConfig`, the `createDomainMapConfig` method, the `JCacheMetrics` and `CacheSimpleConfig` imports. Updated JavaDoc.
- `ArtemisMetricsEndpoint`: removed the parallel JCache section in `cacheMetrics()`.

**Dead-code cleanup that became visible with L2 off:**
- Removed four no-op `clearUserCaches` / `evictUsersFromCache` methods from `UserService`, `UserCreationService`, `UserScheduleService`. Their target IMap (`de.tum.cit.aet.artemis.core.domain.User`, the Hibernate L2 region) is now never populated.
- Removed the unused `UserRepository.findLoginsByGroupName` query that fed `evictUsersFromCache`.
- Updated stale `// L2 cache` comments and JavaDoc in `ResultService.deleteResult`, `UserResource`, and `AdminUserResource`.

**Architecture guardrail:**
- New `ArchitectureTest.testNoHibernateSecondLevelCacheAnnotation` fails the build if any class, field, or method is annotated with `org.hibernate.annotations.Cache`.

**Documentation:**
- New `documentation/docs/developer/guidelines/caching.mdx` — long-form rationale, history, why `READ_WRITE` was rejected, the canonical `TitleCacheEvictionService` pattern, the bar for new caches, scope (what is *not* covered: local in-memory caches and Hazelcast distributed objects), multi-node testing reference, configuration reference. Registered in `sidebar-developer.ts` under Server Guidelines.
- Cross-references added to `server-development.mdx` (next to existing `@Transactional` guidance), `performance.mdx` (end of Data Economy), and `database.mdx` (top-level Callout). Stripped 5 obsolete `@Cache` code examples in `database.mdx` and reframed the L2-cascade discussion.
- Short pointer added to `CLAUDE.md` under Coding Conventions › Java.

### Steps for Testing

This is a server-internal architectural change with no user-facing UI changes. Verification is via the test suites and runtime behaviour on the multi-node stack.

1. Pull the branch.
2. `./gradlew test -x webapp` — full server test suite must pass. In particular:
   - `ArchitectureTest.testNoHibernateSecondLevelCacheAnnotation` (new) confirms no `@Cache` annotation remains.
   - `TitleCacheEvictionServiceTest` (existing) confirms Spring `@Cacheable` + Hibernate event listeners survive without L2.
3. `./run-e2e-tests-local-multinode.sh` — multi-node E2E suite must pass. This is the canonical reproduction surface for cache-coherence regressions; bug `#12574` was originally surfaced by this kind of multi-node exercise.
4. Boot a local stack and exercise FK-heavy reads (course dashboard, exam-for-test-run, communication threads, programming exercises, lectures, admin/users). Watch `/management/prometheus` for `http_server_requests_seconds_max` and `hikaricp_connections_usage_seconds_max` to confirm no regression at the request-level p99.

### Testserver States

You can manage test servers using [Helios](https://helios.aet.cit.tum.de/). Check environment statuses in the [environment list](https://helios.aet.cit.tum.de/repo/69562331/environment/list). To deploy to a test server, go to the [CI/CD](https://helios.aet.cit.tum.de/repo/69562331/ci-cd) page, find your PR or branch, and trigger the deployment.

### Review Progress

#### Code Review
- [x] Code Review 1
- [ ] Code Review 2

#### Manual Tests
- [x] Multi-node E2E green
- [ ] Hot endpoints smoke-tested without latency regression
